exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.why: The foundation squat pattern. Builds the movement before load and is useful for warm ups, high rep BURN work and beginners. Band and pause variations add a twist: mini bands cue the knees out, pulses keep tension, dead stops kill the bounce.
cues: Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out, tripod foot
Sit down between the hips, knees track over the toes
Stand tall and squeeze the glutes
exercises.joint_notes: Generally joint friendly. Use a box with knee pain, heel elevation with stiff ankles.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 12 to 20 reps (or 30 to 40s)
exercises.progress_by: Add a pause, tempo, then load (goblet squat)
exercises.regress_by: Squat to a box, TRX assisted squat

exercises.name: DB Squat to Overhead Press
exercises.why: Links a squat and an overhead press into one total body movement. Very metabolic, great for BURN and HYBRID sessions, and the legs help drive the weight overhead so people can press more.
variation_notes: Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
cues: Squat with the weight in the rack
Drive up hard and use that momentum to press overhead
Lock out with biceps by the ears, ribs down, then lower back to the rack
faults: Pressing before the legs finish the drive
Arching the low back at the top
Losing the rack position and squatting with the elbows dropped
exercises.joint_notes: Needs pain free overhead range. With shoulder pain swap to squat to landmine press. Watch technique as fatigue builds in circuits.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 8 to 12 reps, or 30 to 40s in circuits
exercises.progress_by: Add load, double KBs, barbell, more rounds or density
exercises.regress_by: Goblet squat to press, landmine squat to press, split into separate squat and press

progress_to.name: Double KB Front Squat to Press
Barbell Front Rack Squat to Press

exercises.name: DB Overhead Squat
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, upper back, shoulders, core
exercises.why: The overhead squat exposes stiffness at the ankles, hips, T spine and shoulders all at once, which is why Squat University and the FMS use it as a screen. With a dowel it is an excellent mobility drill; loaded it is a high skill G4 lift.
cues: Arms locked overhead, biceps by the ears, push up into the dowel or weight
Sit down between the hips with the chest proud
Keep the bar over the middle of the foot throughout
faults: Lower back rounding at the bottom
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder demanding: avoid loading with shoulder pain or impingement. Use a dowel as a warm up screen instead.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 5 to 8 reps, light, slow
exercises.progress_by: Dowel → light DB/plate → barbell overhead squat
exercises.regress_by: Dowel only, squat to a box, heels elevated, arms in a Y position

exercises.name: Box Squat
exercises.why: The box sets a consistent, safe depth and teaches people to sit back and control the descent. It is the best teaching squat for beginners and painful knees and, with a barbell or SSB, a classic DeFranco/Westside strength builder.
cues: Box at a height where the spine stays neutral
Sit back and down with control, touch the box lightly (don't crash)
Stay braced, drive up through the whole foot
faults: Plonking down and relaxing on the box
exercises.joint_notes: Excellent for knee pain and older members: adjust height to the pain free range. Lower the box as mobility and control improve.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Lower the box, add load (goblet then SSB/barbell), pause on the box without relaxing, remove the box
exercises.regress_by: Raise the box, TRX assisted box squat, sit to stand

exercises.name: Plate Front Raise Squat
exercises.muscles: Lower and middle traps, rear shoulders, rotator cuff
exercises.why: Small raises in Y, T, W and I shapes strengthen the muscles that control the shoulder blade, especially the lower traps that are often weak in rounded posture. Poliquin's structural balance and Cressey's shoulder programmes rely on them.
cues: Chest supported on an incline bench or lying face down
Thumbs up, lift the arms into the shape using the shoulder blades
Pause 1 to 2s at the top, lower slowly
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder rehab friendly. Use 1 to 3kg or bodyweight.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 per shape, pause at the top
exercises.progress_by: Light DBs, longer pauses
exercises.regress_by: Bodyweight, smaller range

exercises.name: TRX Assisted Squat
exercises.why: Holding the TRX lets people counterbalance, so they can sit deeper and more upright than they could alone. It is the go to G1 squat for beginners, seniors, heavy members and anyone with knee or hip pain, and it builds confidence fast.
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
cues: Hold the handles at chest height with arms straight
Sit back and down, letting the straps take a little weight
Use the legs to stand, the arms only steady you
faults: Pulling with the arms to stand up
Leaning back so far the feet slide
Squatting deeper than the pain free range
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly. Ideal first squat after injury or replacement surgery (within surgeon's limits).
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0
exercises.progress_by: Use the straps less, slower tempo, add a pause, progress to goblet box squat
exercises.regress_by: Squat to a high box with the TRX, reduce depth

exercises.name: Landmine Squat
exercises.why: The landmine's arc lets people lean into the bar and squat with an upright torso and a guided path. It is very back and shoulder friendly and a great bridge between goblet and barbell squatting.
variation_notes: Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn.
cues: Hold the end of the bar at the chest, lean slightly into it
Feet slightly in front of the body, sit down and back
Drive up into the bar, finish tall
faults: Feet too close to the bar so the knees jam
Pushing the bar away with the arms
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder friendly (no bar on the back). Hack squat version loads knees more: control depth with knee pain.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Add plates, add a press at the top, pause reps
exercises.regress_by: Lighter load, reduce depth, goblet box squat

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.why: A simple, joint friendly way to build quad strength and endurance with zero technique demand. Isometrics can reduce knee pain and are ideal for beginners, seniors and anyone who cannot yet squat through full range. The Swiss ball version lets people practise the squat path with support.
cues: Back flat against the wall, feet hip width and slightly in front
Slide down until the knees are at a pain free angle (aim 90 degrees over time)
Weight through the whole foot, breathe slowly, knees in line with toes
faults: Going too deep too soon and aggravating knees
exercises.joint_notes: Very knee friendly at higher positions. Adjust depth to stay at or below 3/10 pain. Avoid long holds with breath holding for members with high blood pressure.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 45s holds, rest 60s, about 70% effort
exercises.progress_by: Lower the position, hold longer, hold a plate, progress to single leg wall sit or tempo goblet squats
exercises.regress_by: Higher position, shorter holds, hands on thighs for the first few sessions

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.why: The classic heavy squat. Builds strength, muscle and bone density (LIFTMOR used heavy squats). Pin and Anderson squats start from the bottom, removing the bounce and building strength out of the hole. At Optimal it is a G4 lift for members with good mobility and no back or shoulder restriction; the SSB is the default alternative.
variation_notes: Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
cues: Bar on the upper back, hands tight, elbows under the bar
Big breath and brace, sit between the hips with knees tracking the toes
Drive up keeping the chest and hips rising together
faults: Hips shooting up first (good morning squat)
Losing the brace and rounding at the bottom
exercises.joint_notes: High spinal load. Not for active back pain. Needs shoulder external rotation to hold the bar: use SSB or trap bar squat if shoulders are cranky.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Add load, pause reps, tempo, 1.25 reps, rep maxes (Teams G4 only)
exercises.regress_by: SSB squat, box squat, goblet or double KB front squat
exercises.group_alternative: Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list

exercises.name: Goblet Squat (KB)
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core
exercises.why: Holding the weight at the chest counterbalances the body, so people naturally squat more upright and deeper with better form. Dan John and Squat University both use it as THE teaching squat, and it is strong enough to stay useful for years. Fits groups perfectly because load scales from a 4kg KB to a 40kg+ DB.
cues: Hold the bell tight to the chest, elbows pointing down
Push the knees out and sit between the hips, chest proud
Drive up through the whole foot, squeeze the glutes at the top
faults: Rounding the upper back and letting the weight pull you forward
Knees caving inward on the way up
exercises.joint_notes: Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat
exercises.regress_by: Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.why: Front loading keeps the torso upright, puts more work on the quads and core, and puts less shear on the low back than back squatting. The double KB front squat is a great G3 group squat; the barbell front squat is a G4 strength lift for those with the wrist and thoracic mobility.
variation_notes: Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
cues: Bells or bar in a tight rack, elbows high and forward
Brace, sit straight down between the hips
Keep the elbows up as you drive up
faults: Elbows dropping and the chest falling forward
exercises.joint_notes: Low back friendlier than back squats. Barbell front rack needs wrist, lat and T spine mobility. Zercher loads the elbows: use padding.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Add load, pause at the bottom, tempo, progress DB → double KB → barbell front squat
exercises.regress_by: Goblet squat, box to control depth, lighter load
exercises.group_alternative: Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list

exercises.name: Cyclist Squat
exercises.why: A narrow stance, heels elevated squat that lets the knees travel well forward. It biases the quads (especially the inner quad) with an upright torso, so it is easy on the low back and great for knee health and quad size. A Poliquin and Squat University favourite.
cues: Heels on a wedge or plate, feet close together
Hold a weight at the chest, stay tall
Knees travel forward over the toes, sit straight down, control the bottom
exercises.joint_notes: Very low back friendly. Knees work hard in deep flexion, so build depth gradually for sensitive knees.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
exercises.progress_by: Add load (DB/KB then SSB), slower tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps
exercises.regress_by: Lower heel height, squat to a box, bodyweight with TRX support

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Squat
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, upper back, shoulders, core
exercises.why: The overhead squat exposes stiffness at the ankles, hips, T spine and shoulders all at once, which is why Squat University and the FMS use it as a screen. With a dowel it is an excellent mobility drill; loaded it is a high skill G4 lift.
variation_notes: Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
cues: Arms locked overhead, biceps by the ears, push up into the dowel or weight
Sit down between the hips with the chest proud
Keep the bar over the middle of the foot throughout
faults: Lower back rounding at the bottom
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder demanding: avoid loading with shoulder pain or impingement. Use a dowel as a warm up screen instead.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 5 to 8 reps, light, slow
exercises.progress_by: Dowel → light DB/plate → barbell overhead squat
exercises.regress_by: Dowel only, squat to a box, heels elevated, arms in a Y position
exercises.group_alternative: Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list

exercises.name: Spanish Squat (Band)
exercises.why: A band behind the knees lets the shins stay vertical while the hips sit back, so the quads work hard with very little compressive stress on the front of the knee. Isometric holds like this are one of the best known tools for calming irritable knees (patellar tendon and kneecap pain) while still loading the quads. A Squat University and physio favourite.
cues: Heavy band behind both knees anchored to the rig, walk back until it is tight
Sit back and down until thighs are around 60 to 90 degrees, shins vertical
Keep chest proud, push knees back into the band and hold
faults: Letting the knees drift forward off the band
Holding the breath for the whole set
Going so deep that pain rises above 3/10
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly by design. Often reduces knee pain for several hours afterwards, which makes it a great warm up before squatting for sore knees. Back is upright so low back load is minimal.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 45s holds, rest 60s, about 70% effort (5 x 45s is a classic tendon dose)
exercises.progress_by: Hold longer (45s), sit deeper, add a weight held at the chest, progress to tempo goblet squats and Poliquin step ups
exercises.regress_by: Shorten the hold, sit less deep, lighter band, switch to a wall sit with a higher position

Sit down between the hips, knees track over the toes
Stand tall and squeeze the glutes
exercises.joint_notes: Generally joint friendly. Use a box with knee pain, heel elevation with stiff ankles.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 12 to 20 reps (or 30 to 40s)
exercises.progress_by: Add a pause, tempo, then load (goblet squat)
exercises.regress_by: Squat to a box, TRX assisted squat

exercises.name: Banded Barbell Box Squat
exercises.why: The box sets a consistent, safe depth and teaches people to sit back and control the descent. It is the best teaching squat for beginners and painful knees and, with a barbell or SSB, a classic DeFranco/Westside strength builder.
variation_notes: Band resistance gets harder at the top (accommodating resistance) and can cue better positions such as knees out.

cues: Box at a height where the spine stays neutral
Sit back and down with control, touch the box lightly (don't crash)
Stay braced, drive up through the whole foot
faults: Plonking down and relaxing on the box
exercises.joint_notes: Excellent for knee pain and older members: adjust height to the pain free range. Lower the box as mobility and control improve.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Lower the box, add load (goblet then SSB/barbell), pause on the box without relaxing, remove the box
exercises.regress_by: Raise the box, TRX assisted box squat, sit to stand

exercises.name: Sissy Squat (Assisted)
exercises.muscles: Quads (rectus femoris in a lengthened position), hip flexors
exercises.why: Trains the quads with the knees travelling far over the toes and the hips extended. Builds strength in the end range of knee bending, which Ben Patrick uses to bulletproof knees. Assisted versions are surprisingly accessible.
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
cues: Hold a post or TRX for support
Rise onto the toes, push the knees forward and lean the body back as one straight line from knee to shoulder
Lower only as far as pain free, drive back up through the quads
faults: Bending at the hips (turns it into a normal squat)
Letting go of the support before ready
exercises.joint_notes: Earn it. Start short range with hand support. Avoid with acute knee pain, recent knee surgery or knee replacements unless cleared.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 12 reps, slow lowering, hand support
exercises.progress_by: Increase range, reduce hand assistance, add a plate at the chest, progress towards reverse Nordic
exercises.regress_by: Short range only, more hand support, swap to Spanish squat or heels elevated goblet squat

exercises.name: Cable Squat to Row
exercises.muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
exercises.why: Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
variation_notes: Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
cues: Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow
Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back)
Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch
exercises.joint_notes: Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps
exercises.regress_by: Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row

exercises.name: Isometric Squat Hold
exercises.why: A simple, joint friendly way to build quad strength and endurance with zero technique demand. Isometrics can reduce knee pain and are ideal for beginners, seniors and anyone who cannot yet squat through full range. The Swiss ball version lets people practise the squat path with support.
variation_notes: Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
cues: Back flat against the wall, feet hip width and slightly in front
Slide down until the knees are at a pain free angle (aim 90 degrees over time)
Weight through the whole foot, breathe slowly, knees in line with toes
faults: Going too deep too soon and aggravating knees
exercises.joint_notes: Very knee friendly at higher positions. Adjust depth to stay at or below 3/10 pain. Avoid long holds with breath holding for members with high blood pressure.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 45s holds, rest 60s, about 70% effort
exercises.progress_by: Lower the position, hold longer, hold a plate, progress to single leg wall sit or tempo goblet squats
exercises.regress_by: Higher position, shorter holds, hands on thighs for the first few sessions

exercises.why: A wide stance with toes turned out shifts work towards the inner thighs and glutes and lets people with limited ankle mobility squat deeper with an upright chest. Useful variety and a gentler squat for some knees and hips.
cues: Feet wide, toes turned out about 30 degrees
Knees push out over the toes, sit straight down
Squeeze the glutes and inner thighs to stand
faults: Going wider than the hips allow
Rounding to reach the weight to the floor
exercises.joint_notes: Avoid very wide stances with hip pain or groin strains. Good for members whose ankles limit a normal squat.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
exercises.progress_by: Add load, stand on two boxes for a deficit, pause at the bottom
exercises.regress_by: Bodyweight, reduce depth, squat to a box

exercises.name: Narrow Stance Goblet Squat
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core
exercises.why: Holding the weight at the chest counterbalances the body, so people naturally squat more upright and deeper with better form. Dan John and Squat University both use it as THE teaching squat, and it is strong enough to stay useful for years. Fits groups perfectly because load scales from a 4kg KB to a 40kg+ DB.
cues: Hold the bell tight to the chest, elbows pointing down
Push the knees out and sit between the hips, chest proud
Drive up through the whole foot, squeeze the glutes at the top
faults: Rounding the upper back and letting the weight pull you forward
Knees caving inward on the way up
exercises.joint_notes: Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat
exercises.regress_by: Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell

exercises.name: Wide Stance Barbell Squat
exercises.why: The classic heavy squat. Builds strength, muscle and bone density (LIFTMOR used heavy squats). Pin and Anderson squats start from the bottom, removing the bounce and building strength out of the hole. At Optimal it is a G4 lift for members with good mobility and no back or shoulder restriction; the SSB is the default alternative.
variation_notes: Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
Wide grip/stance shifts emphasis (chest/upper back or adductors) and can be less friendly for some shoulders and hips.
cues: Bar on the upper back, hands tight, elbows under the bar
Big breath and brace, sit between the hips with knees tracking the toes
Drive up keeping the chest and hips rising together
faults: Hips shooting up first (good morning squat)
Losing the brace and rounding at the bottom
exercises.joint_notes: High spinal load. Not for active back pain. Needs shoulder external rotation to hold the bar: use SSB or trap bar squat if shoulders are cranky.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Add load, pause reps, tempo, 1.25 reps, rep maxes (Teams G4 only)
exercises.regress_by: SSB squat, box squat, goblet or double KB front squat
exercises.group_alternative: Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list

exercises.name: Double KB Front Rack Squat
exercises.why: Front loading keeps the torso upright, puts more work on the quads and core, and puts less shear on the low back than back squatting. The double KB front squat is a great G3 group squat; the barbell front squat is a G4 strength lift for those with the wrist and thoracic mobility.
variation_notes: Double KB: heavier total load plus a front rack or bilateral grip demand.
cues: Bells or bar in a tight rack, elbows high and forward
Brace, sit straight down between the hips
Keep the elbows up as you drive up
faults: Elbows dropping and the chest falling forward
exercises.joint_notes: Low back friendlier than back squats. Barbell front rack needs wrist, lat and T spine mobility. Zercher loads the elbows: use padding.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Add load, pause at the bottom, tempo, progress DB → double KB → barbell front squat
exercises.regress_by: Goblet squat, box to control depth, lighter load

exercises.name: Double KB Front Squat to Press
exercises.why: Links a squat and an overhead press into one total body movement. Very metabolic, great for BURN and HYBRID sessions, and the legs help drive the weight overhead so people can press more.
variation_notes: Double KB: heavier total load plus a front rack or bilateral grip demand.
Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
cues: Squat with the weight in the rack
Drive up hard and use that momentum to press overhead
Lock out with biceps by the ears, ribs down, then lower back to the rack
faults: Pressing before the legs finish the drive
Arching the low back at the top
Losing the rack position and squatting with the elbows dropped
exercises.joint_notes: Needs pain free overhead range. With shoulder pain swap to squat to landmine press. Watch technique as fatigue builds in circuits.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 8 to 12 reps, or 30 to 40s in circuits
exercises.progress_by: Add load, double KBs, barbell, more rounds or density
exercises.regress_by: Goblet squat to press, landmine squat to press, split into separate squat and press
exercises.group_alternative: Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list
same_level_swaps: Barbell Front Rack Squat to Press

exercises.name: Squat to Box Stand Up (Bodyweight)
exercises.why: The most important real life squat: getting up from a chair or toilet. A key longevity skill and a core test for seniors (30 second sit to stand). Done fast on the way up, it trains power, which declines faster than strength with age.
variation_notes: Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
cues: Sit tall on a box or chair, feet slightly back under the knees
Lean the chest forward, push the floor away and stand up tall
Sit back down slowly with control, don't flop
faults: Using the hands to push off
Collapsing back down onto the seat
exercises.joint_notes: Suitable for almost everyone. Raise the seat height for painful knees or hips. Single leg version needs good knee control.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps (or max reps in 30s for testing), stand up fast, lower slowly
exercises.progress_by: Lower the box, hold a weight at the chest, stand up as fast as possible (power), single leg sit to stand
exercises.regress_by: Raise the seat, use hands on thighs or a TRX for help, reduce reps

exercises.name: Split Squat (Bodyweight)
exercises.why: The entry point of the single leg ladder. A static split stance gives a stable base, so people learn to load one leg at a time safely. It builds balance, fixes imbalances and is far easier on the back than heavy bilateral squats. Front foot elevated adds knee travel (ATG style); cable and landmine versions add stability.
cues: Long split stance, both feet pointing forward, hip width apart
Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor
Push through the front foot to stand, keep the torso tall
faults: Lunging forward instead of dropping down
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly when depth is controlled. Use a pad under the back knee. Hold a support for balance in seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Add load, elevate the front foot (ATG style), then elevate the back foot (RFESS)
exercises.regress_by: TRX or rig assisted split squat, shorter range, isometric split squat hold

exercises.name: Barbell Walking Lunge
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance, grip when loaded
exercises.why: Forward and walking lunges add deceleration and balance: you have to control the body moving forward over the front leg. Very functional and very metabolic, so they suit BURN and HYBRID sessions. Loaded carry lunges add grip and core.
variation_notes: Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
cues: Long step forward, land heel first
Drop the back knee down, front knee over the middle of the foot
Push through the front foot and step through to the next rep
faults: Short choppy steps that load the front knee
exercises.joint_notes: More knee stress than reverse lunges. Swap to reverse lunges or split squats with knee pain. Needs space in groups.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg) or 20 to 30m
exercises.progress_by: Add load (DB, KB rack, overhead), pulses, longer distance
exercises.regress_by: Reverse lunge, split squat, hand support

exercises.name: Slider Reverse Lunge
exercises.why: Stepping backwards keeps the shin more vertical, so it is far kinder to the knees than forward lunges while still training single leg strength and balance. The default lunge at Optimal. Deficit and slider versions increase range and control.
variation_notes: Sliders add a friction based eccentric control challenge.
cues: Stand tall, step one foot back
Drop the back knee towards the floor, front shin fairly vertical
Drive through the front heel to stand back up
exercises.joint_notes: Most knee friendly lunge. Use a pad and hand support for beginners.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Add load, deficit (front foot on a plate), knee drive at the top, barbell/landmine
exercises.regress_by: Split squat (static), hand support, shorter range

exercises.name: Box Step Up (Bodyweight)
exercises.why: A real life movement (stairs, kerbs, climbing). Very back friendly, easy to scale by box height, and the concentric emphasis means little soreness. Knee drive and crossover versions add balance and hip work.
cues: Whole foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot
Lean forward slightly and drive through the box leg to stand tall
Step down with control, don't push off the bottom leg
faults: Box too high so the hip hikes
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly at lower heights. Use a low box and hand support for seniors and knee pain. Faster 'step ups' in BURN keep impact low.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Higher box, add DBs/goblet/barbell, add a knee drive, slower lowering
exercises.regress_by: Lower box, hand support, bodyweight

exercises.name: Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat (Bodyweight)
exercises.pattern: Single leg: split squat (rear foot elevated)
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, adductors, hip flexor stretch on the back leg
exercises.why: Mike Boyle's signature lower body lift. Huge leg strength with far less spinal load than heavy bilateral squats, fixes left/right differences, and stretches the back leg's hip flexor (great for desk workers). Lean forward slightly for more glutes, stay upright for more quads.
cues: Back foot laces down on a bench, front foot far enough forward that the front heel stays down
Drop the back knee straight down, front knee tracks over the toes
Drive through the front foot, keep the hips square
faults: Front foot too close so the heel lifts
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly when the depth is controlled. A lower bench helps tight hip flexors. Balance can limit beginners: hold the rig with one hand.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Add load (DBs, then double KB rack, landmine, SSB/barbell), pause, 1.5 reps, deficit (front foot on a plate)
exercises.regress_by: Split squat with back foot on the floor, hand support, reduce depth

exercises.name: Low Box Step Down
exercises.why: Controlled lowering from a step builds knee control and eccentric quad strength, the exact quality needed for walking downstairs. Also a key screening test for knee valgus and hip control.
cues: Stand on a box, other leg hanging off the front or side
Lower slowly by bending the standing knee, hips back slightly
Tap the heel lightly and return without pushing off the floor
faults: Hip dropping on the free side
exercises.joint_notes: Excellent for knee rehab when the box is low. Raise the height as control improves.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 each leg, 3s lowering
exercises.progress_by: Higher box, hold weight, slower lowering
exercises.regress_by: Lower box, hand support, Poliquin step up

exercises.name: Poliquin Step Up
exercises.pattern: Single leg: knee over toes step (VMO)
exercises.why: Low step variations where the knee deliberately travels forward over the toes with the heel raised (Poliquin step up) or from the toes (Patrick step). They load the inner quad and patellar tendon in a controlled way, which is why Poliquin, Ben Patrick and physios use them for knee pain and knee resilience. Small range, huge payoff.
cues: Stand on a low step, working heel raised on a small plate or wedge (Poliquin) or on the toes (Patrick)
Slowly lower the other heel towards the floor by bending the working knee forward over the toes
Lightly tap and drive back up through the front of the foot, keeping the knee in line
faults: Hips shifting back instead of the knee travelling forward
Dropping fast instead of controlling the lowering
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly when kept pain free. Start with a very low step (5 to 10cm) and hand support. Ideal in every knee pain programme.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each leg, slow lowering (3s)
exercises.progress_by: Higher step, slower tempo, hold DBs, progress to step downs and front foot elevated split squats
exercises.regress_by: Lower step, hand on the rig, partial range

exercises.name: Barbell Split Squat
exercises.why: The entry point of the single leg ladder. A static split stance gives a stable base, so people learn to load one leg at a time safely. It builds balance, fixes imbalances and is far easier on the back than heavy bilateral squats. Front foot elevated adds knee travel (ATG style); cable and landmine versions add stability.
variation_notes: Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
cues: Long split stance, both feet pointing forward, hip width apart
Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor
Push through the front foot to stand, keep the torso tall
faults: Lunging forward instead of dropping down
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly when depth is controlled. Use a pad under the back knee. Hold a support for balance in seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Add load, elevate the front foot (ATG style), then elevate the back foot (RFESS)
exercises.regress_by: TRX or rig assisted split squat, shorter range, isometric split squat hold

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat Jump (Light)
exercises.muscles: Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
exercises.why: Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
variation_notes: Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes
Stick the landing for a second before the next rep
Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops
faults: Landing stiff legged or with knees caving
Too many reps (plyos are not cardio)
exercises.joint_notes: IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.

exercises.name: Hip Hinge Dowel Drill
exercises.why: Teaches people to move at the hips not the spine. The dowel gives instant feedback (head, upper back and tailbone stay in contact). Every hinge exercise depends on this skill, so McGill and Squat University teach it first.

Soft knees, push the hips back as if closing a car door with your bum
Hinge until you feel the hamstrings, keep all three contact points, stand back up
faults: Losing the dowel contact at the low back
Bending the knees into a squat
Looking up and cranking the neck
exercises.joint_notes: Ideal for back pain members. No load, no risk.

exercises.progress_by: Hold a KB at the chest, progress to KB deadlift from blocks
exercises.regress_by: Hinge to a wall (bum touches the wall) with a smaller range

exercises.name: KB Swing (Two Hand)
exercises.muscles: Glutes, hamstrings, core, grip, cardiovascular system
exercises.why: The king of hinge conditioning (Dan John, Pavel). Trains explosive hip extension (power) and heart rate at the same time with no impact on the knees. Excellent for fat loss, posture and glute strength. Dead stop versions teach control; single arm versions add anti rotation.
cues: Hike the bell back high between the thighs
Snap the hips forward, squeeze the glutes, let the bell float to chest height
Let it fall, hinge late, keep the spine neutral
faults: Squatting the swing instead of hinging
exercises.joint_notes: Back friendly when the hinge is good. Teach the KB deadlift first. Not for acute low back pain. American (overhead) swings stress shoulders and low back: use hip height swings instead.
exercises.prescription: 4 to 10 sets x 10 to 20 reps, or EMOM; 'hike, snap, float'
exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, single arm, alternating, swings EMOM, heavier with fewer reps for power
exercises.regress_by: KB deadlift, dead stop swing, lighter bell, cable pull through

Keep the spine long and neutral
Stand up by driving the hips forward

exercises.joint_notes: Loaded good mornings are not for low back pain. Keep loads light and range controlled for 40+.

exercises.progress_by: Band → light barbell → SSB good morning, tempo, pause
exercises.regress_by: Bodyweight, dowel hinge drill

exercises.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
exercises.why: The RDL starts from the top and lowers the weight by pushing the hips back, so it builds hamstrings and glutes in a lengthened position with low skill demand. It's the best hamstring builder for most members and a staple for posture and back resilience.
cues: Soft knees, weight close to the legs
Push the hips back, slide the weight down the thighs, keep the back flat
Stop when the hamstrings are tight (usually mid shin), drive the hips forward to stand
faults: Rounding the back to go lower
Squatting it by bending the knees too much
Weight drifting away from the legs
exercises.joint_notes: Back friendly with good form and controlled range. Reduce range for tight hamstrings or low back sensitivity.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: DB → double KB → trap bar → barbell RDL, tempo (4s lowering), pauses, deficit
exercises.regress_by: KB deadlift from blocks, cable pull through, hinge dowel drill, reduce range

cues: Feet flat, shins vertical at the top
Tuck the ribs down, drive through the heels and squeeze the glutes to lift
Pause at the top without arching the low back, lower slowly
faults: Arching the low back instead of extending the hips
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly. Use a pad on the hips when loaded. Shoulder elevated versions need a stable bench.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (pause 1 to 2s at the top)
exercises.progress_by: Bridge → hip thrust off a bench → load (DB, barbell) → single leg, add pauses or bands

exercises.why: Bridges and hip thrusts train the glutes at their strongest point (full hip extension) with almost no spinal load. They are essential for back pain, knee pain, posture, sprinting and golf power, and are safe for nearly everyone. Single leg versions fix imbalances.
variation_notes: Weighted: progress to this once 12 to 15 bodyweight reps are easy.
cues: Feet flat, shins vertical at the top
Tuck the ribs down, drive through the heels and squeeze the glutes to lift
Pause at the top without arching the low back, lower slowly
faults: Arching the low back instead of extending the hips
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly. Use a pad on the hips when loaded. Shoulder elevated versions need a stable bench.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (pause 1 to 2s at the top)
exercises.progress_by: Bridge → hip thrust off a bench → load (DB, barbell) → single leg, add pauses or bands

exercises.name: Double KB Romanian Deadlift

variation_notes: Double KB: heavier total load plus a front rack or bilateral grip demand.

Push the hips back, slide the weight down the thighs, keep the back flat

Squatting it by bending the knees too much
Weight drifting away from the legs

exercises.name: Swiss Ball Hamstring Curl
exercises.why: Hamstrings both extend the hip and bend the knee; curls train the knee bending role that RDLs miss. Strong hamstrings protect knees and reduce hamstring strain risk. Nordic curls are among the best researched injury prevention exercises.
variation_notes: Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
cues: Lie on your back, heels on the ball/sliders/TRX, lift the hips
Curl the heels towards the bum keeping the hips high
Extend slowly back out (control is the exercise)
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly. Nordics are demanding: use band assistance and partial range, expect soreness at first.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
exercises.progress_by: Hips stay up throughout, single leg, slower lowering, Nordic progression
exercises.regress_by: Hips on the floor curl, eccentric only, double leg

exercises.name: Jefferson Curl (Light)
exercises.muscles: Spinal erectors and hamstrings in a lengthened position

Tuck the chin and roll down slowly, one segment at a time
Roll back up from the bottom, slow and controlled
faults: Doing it when the back is irritated

exercises.regress_by: Seated good morning (ATG), cat cow, toe touch to squat

exercises.name: Clean Pull (Barbell)
exercises.muscles: Whole body: glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders
exercises.why: Explosive triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) trains power and rate of force development. Power declines faster than strength with age, so it must be trained, but the skill demand is high. DB, KB and landmine versions are far easier to learn and safer for groups than barbell versions.
variation_notes: Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
cues: Start in a strong hinge with the weight close
Explode up through the legs and hips, shrug and pull the elbows high
Catch softly in a strong rack position (or overhead), stand tall
faults: Weight swinging away from the body
exercises.joint_notes: Wrists, shoulders and low back need to be healthy. Barbell versions: Teams G4 only. Not for osteoporosis without careful progression.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
exercises.progress_by: Pull → hang version → from the floor; DB → KB → barbell
exercises.regress_by: Pull only (no catch), KB swing, med ball scoop toss, landmine clean
exercises.group_alternative: Teams only (heavy or high skill): in groups use a G3 regression from the Regress to list

Hinge back letting the rope pull the hips back
Drive the hips through and squeeze the glutes, stand tall
exercises.joint_notes: Very back friendly. A great swing and deadlift regression.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, pause at the top, progress to KB swing
exercises.regress_by: Band version, shorter range

exercises.name: Landmine Deadlift

Grip, pull the shoulders down, brace
Push the floor away and stand tall, squeeze the glutes

exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, double KB, lower to the floor, progress to RDL, swing and trap bar
exercises.regress_by: Bell on a block/step, hinge drill

exercises.name: Double KB Swing
exercises.muscles: Glutes, hamstrings, core, grip, cardiovascular system
exercises.why: The king of hinge conditioning (Dan John, Pavel). Trains explosive hip extension (power) and heart rate at the same time with no impact on the knees. Excellent for fat loss, posture and glute strength. Dead stop versions teach control; single arm versions add anti rotation.
variation_notes: Double KB: heavier total load plus a front rack or bilateral grip demand.
cues: Hike the bell back high between the thighs
Snap the hips forward, squeeze the glutes, let the bell float to chest height
Let it fall, hinge late, keep the spine neutral
faults: Squatting the swing instead of hinging
exercises.joint_notes: Back friendly when the hinge is good. Teach the KB deadlift first. Not for acute low back pain. American (overhead) swings stress shoulders and low back: use hip height swings instead.
exercises.prescription: 4 to 10 sets x 10 to 20 reps, or EMOM; 'hike, snap, float'
exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, single arm, alternating, swings EMOM, heavier with fewer reps for power
exercises.regress_by: KB deadlift, dead stop swing, lighter bell, cable pull through
same_level_swaps: Single Arm KB Swing to Catch

exercises.name: Single Leg RDL (Bodyweight)
exercises.muscles: Hamstrings, glutes (incl. glute med), foot and ankle stability
exercises.why: Single leg hinges build hamstring and glute strength, balance and hip stability one side at a time, and they spare the spine because loads are lighter. Kickstand and B stance versions give a stepping stone with the back foot for support. Hip airplanes train hip rotation control (great for golf).
cues: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, other leg reaching back
Hinge forward as one straight line from head to heel, hips square
Drive the standing heel into the floor and squeeze the glute to stand
faults: Hips opening up (rotating) towards the ceiling
Rounding the back to reach the floor
exercises.joint_notes: Back friendly. Balance limits load: use a support or kickstand first. Excellent for golfers and runners.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Kickstand → full single leg, add load (DB/KB, double KB, landmine), slower tempo, add a row or reach
exercises.regress_by: Supported single leg RDL (hand on rig), kickstand RDL, bodyweight

exercises.name: Single Arm KB Swing

exercises.name: Wall Press Up

exercises.why: A moving plank: chest and arm strength plus core control. The shoulder blades move freely, which is healthier for shoulders than bench pressing. Easy to scale by hand height so every level in a group can do the same exercise. Push up plus adds serratus work for shoulder health.
cues: Hands just outside shoulders, body in a straight line, glutes and abs tight
Lower the chest between the hands, elbows about 45 degrees from the body
Push the floor away until arms are straight and the upper back is spread
exercises.joint_notes: Wrist pain: use DB handles or fists. Shoulder pain: elevate the hands and keep elbows tucked.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 6 to 15 reps (or total reps progression)
exercises.progress_by: Lower the hand height (wall → bench → box → floor), tempo, pause, feet elevated, add a weighted vest/plate
exercises.regress_by: Higher incline (bench or wall), knee push up, shorter range

Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn.
cues: Hold the end of the bar at the shoulder, ribs down, glutes tight
Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around
Lower with control back to the shoulder
exercises.joint_notes: Best press for shoulder pain and limited overhead range.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each arm)
exercises.progress_by: Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, two hands, half kneeling

exercises.name: Press Up Plus
exercises.why: The serratus holds the shoulder blade against the ribcage and rotates it upward for overhead reaching. Weak serratus = winging and shoulder pain.
cues: Arms straight
Push the floor or weight away, spreading the shoulder blades
Return slowly
exercises.joint_notes: Very shoulder friendly.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
exercises.progress_by: Push up plus, band punch, heavier
exercises.regress_by: Wall version

Press forward until arms are straight, keep the ribs down
Return with control

exercises.name: TRX Row
exercises.muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, core
exercises.why: Pulling your own bodyweight in a plank position. The angle sets the difficulty, so it scales from total beginner (standing upright) to advanced (feet elevated) in the same station. A core Optimal group exercise and part of Ed's screening (TRX row at 45 degrees).
cues: Body in a straight line, heels down
Pull the chest to the handles, shoulder blades back and down
Lower slowly to straight arms
faults: Shrugging or poking the chin forward
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder friendly. Neutral grip TRX handles are easiest on elbows.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 15 reps (or total reps progression), pause at the top
exercises.progress_by: Walk the feet forward (more horizontal), feet elevated, single arm, pause/tempo
exercises.regress_by: Stand more upright, step back, scapular retraction only (G1 of the Optimal screen)
same_level_swaps: Inverted Row to Pull Up Progression

exercises.name: Wide Grip Cable Row
exercises.muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
exercises.why: Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
variation_notes: Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
Wide grip/stance shifts emphasis (chest/upper back or adductors) and can be less friendly for some shoulders and hips.
cues: Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow
Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back)
Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch
exercises.joint_notes: Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps
exercises.regress_by: Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row

variation_notes: Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
cues: Arms straight in front, slight bend in the elbows
Pull the hands apart until the band touches the chest, squeeze the shoulder blades
Return slowly
exercises.joint_notes: Very shoulder friendly.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 15 to 25 reps
exercises.progress_by: Heavier band, pauses, different angles (overhand, underhand, diagonal)
exercises.regress_by: Lighter band

exercises.name: KB Gorilla Row
exercises.muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
exercises.why: Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.

Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back)

exercises.regress_by: Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row

Place it down with control, alternate

exercises.name: KB High Pull
exercises.muscles: Whole body: glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders
exercises.why: Explosive triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) trains power and rate of force development. Power declines faster than strength with age, so it must be trained, but the skill demand is high. DB, KB and landmine versions are far easier to learn and safer for groups than barbell versions.
cues: Start in a strong hinge with the weight close
Explode up through the legs and hips, shrug and pull the elbows high
Catch softly in a strong rack position (or overhead), stand tall
faults: Weight swinging away from the body
exercises.joint_notes: Wrists, shoulders and low back need to be healthy. Barbell versions: Teams G4 only. Not for osteoporosis without careful progression.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
exercises.progress_by: Pull → hang version → from the floor; DB → KB → barbell
exercises.regress_by: Pull only (no catch), KB swing, med ball scoop toss, landmine clean

exercises.name: Sled Row (Rope)
exercises.pattern: Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
exercises.why: The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
cues: Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet
Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes)
Keep steady steps and a neutral spine
faults: Hips too high or too low
Taking huge steps that slow the sled
exercises.joint_notes: Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
exercises.prescription: 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
exercises.progress_by: More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, slower, shorter distance

exercises.name: Band Resisted Inverted Row
exercises.muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, core
exercises.why: Pulling your own bodyweight in a plank position. The angle sets the difficulty, so it scales from total beginner (standing upright) to advanced (feet elevated) in the same station. A core Optimal group exercise and part of Ed's screening (TRX row at 45 degrees).
variation_notes: Band resistance gets harder at the top (accommodating resistance) and can cue better positions such as knees out.
cues: Body in a straight line, heels down
Pull the chest to the handles, shoulder blades back and down
Lower slowly to straight arms
faults: Shrugging or poking the chin forward
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder friendly. Neutral grip TRX handles are easiest on elbows.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 15 reps (or total reps progression), pause at the top
exercises.progress_by: Walk the feet forward (more horizontal), feet elevated, single arm, pause/tempo
exercises.regress_by: Stand more upright, step back, scapular retraction only (G1 of the Optimal screen)

exercises.name: Wall Slide
exercises.muscles: Lower traps, serratus, T spine extension
exercises.why: Sliding the arms up the wall trains the shoulder blade to rotate upward properly, which is key for pain free overhead movement. Part of the Simple 6 style warm up.
cues: Back or forearms against the wall, ribs down
Slide the arms up keeping contact, shoulders down
Slide back down, squeezing the shoulder blades
exercises.joint_notes: Very shoulder friendly.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Add a band or lift off at the top
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range, floor angels

exercises.name: Tall Kneeling Landmine Press
exercises.why: The landmine press moves on an arc between a horizontal and vertical press, letting the shoulder blade move freely. It is the most shoulder friendly way to press overhead and the go to for members who can't press straight overhead (Cressey). Half kneeling adds core and hip stability.
variation_notes: Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn.
Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
cues: Hold the end of the bar at the shoulder, ribs down, glutes tight
Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around
Lower with control back to the shoulder
exercises.joint_notes: Best press for shoulder pain and limited overhead range.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each arm)
exercises.progress_by: Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, two hands, half kneeling

exercises.name: Pike Press Up
exercises.why: Bodyweight overhead pressing progressions. High skill and high shoulder load; good for strong, healthy shoulders only.
cues: Hips high, hands shoulder width
Lower the head between the hands
Press back up, keep the core tight
exercises.joint_notes: Avoid with shoulder pain, high blood pressure (inverted), glaucoma.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 5 to 10
exercises.progress_by: Elevate the feet, wall handstand holds
exercises.regress_by: Pike from knees, DB overhead press

exercises.why: The get up teaches you to get up from the floor while holding a weight overhead: shoulder stability, hip mobility and confidence in one. Getting off the floor is a key longevity skill (Attia, Dan John, Pavel). Windmills and arm bars build shoulder stability and hip hinge mobility.
cues: Eyes on the bell, arm locked
Move through each step slowly: roll to elbow, hand, high bridge, sweep the leg, kneel, stand
Reverse every step with control
exercises.joint_notes: Learn with a shoe or no weight first. Shoulder pain: half get up with no load only.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 reps each side, slow
exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, full get up
exercises.regress_by: Half get up, shoe on the fist, no weight

exercises.name: KB Thruster
exercises.why: Links a squat and an overhead press into one total body movement. Very metabolic, great for BURN and HYBRID sessions, and the legs help drive the weight overhead so people can press more.
cues: Squat with the weight in the rack
Drive up hard and use that momentum to press overhead
Lock out with biceps by the ears, ribs down, then lower back to the rack
faults: Pressing before the legs finish the drive
Arching the low back at the top
Losing the rack position and squatting with the elbows dropped
exercises.joint_notes: Needs pain free overhead range. With shoulder pain swap to squat to landmine press. Watch technique as fatigue builds in circuits.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 8 to 12 reps, or 30 to 40s in circuits
exercises.progress_by: Add load, double KBs, barbell, more rounds or density
exercises.regress_by: Goblet squat to press, landmine squat to press, split into separate squat and press

progress_to.name: Double KB Front Squat to Press
Barbell Front Rack Squat to Press

exercises.name: Handstand Hold (Wall)
exercises.why: Bodyweight overhead pressing progressions. High skill and high shoulder load; good for strong, healthy shoulders only.
cues: Hips high, hands shoulder width
Lower the head between the hands
Press back up, keep the core tight
exercises.joint_notes: Avoid with shoulder pain, high blood pressure (inverted), glaucoma.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 5 to 10
exercises.progress_by: Elevate the feet, wall handstand holds
exercises.regress_by: Pike from knees, DB overhead press

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.why: Pressing overhead builds shoulder strength and the ability to put things on high shelves (a real life task). LIFTMOR used overhead presses for spinal bone density. Requires overhead mobility; half kneeling and single arm versions add core demand and are often easier on the low back.
variation_notes: Barbell: allows the heaviest loading for maximum strength and bone stimulus; earn it with technique (usually G3 to G4, Teams).
cues: Ribs down, glutes tight, wrist stacked over the elbow
Press up and slightly back so the biceps finish by the ears
Lower with control to the shoulder
faults: Arching the low back to get the weight up
exercises.joint_notes: Needs pain free overhead range (wall test). Shoulder pain: landmine press. Behind the neck pressing: avoid for 40+.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Seated → half kneeling → standing → push press; heavier, single arm, bottoms up
exercises.regress_by: Landmine press, high incline DB press, lighter weights

Lower behind the head with control
Extend fully, squeeze
exercises.joint_notes: Elbow pain: use a rope or band, lighter.

exercises.progress_by: Heavier, slower
exercises.regress_by: Band, lighter

exercises.name: Behind the Neck Press (Light)
exercises.why: Dynamic drills raise temperature, take joints through range and rehearse patterns (RAMP warm up). The World's Greatest Stretch hits hip flexors, hamstrings, adductors and T spine in one move. 40+ members need a full 8 to 10 minute warm up every session.
variation_notes: Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Move through big comfortable ranges
Increase range each rep
Breathe and stay controlled
exercises.joint_notes: Safe for almost everyone.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 x 5 to 10 each side (or 20 to 30m)
exercises.progress_by: Bigger range, add reaches
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range, hand support

exercises.name: Landmine Press
exercises.why: The landmine press moves on an arc between a horizontal and vertical press, letting the shoulder blade move freely. It is the most shoulder friendly way to press overhead and the go to for members who can't press straight overhead (Cressey). Half kneeling adds core and hip stability.
variation_notes: Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn.
cues: Hold the end of the bar at the shoulder, ribs down, glutes tight
Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around
Lower with control back to the shoulder
exercises.joint_notes: Best press for shoulder pain and limited overhead range.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each arm)
exercises.progress_by: Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, two hands, half kneeling

exercises.name: KB Clean and Press
exercises.muscles: Whole body: glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders
exercises.why: Explosive triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) trains power and rate of force development. Power declines faster than strength with age, so it must be trained, but the skill demand is high. DB, KB and landmine versions are far easier to learn and safer for groups than barbell versions.
variation_notes: Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
cues: Start in a strong hinge with the weight close
Explode up through the legs and hips, shrug and pull the elbows high
Catch softly in a strong rack position (or overhead), stand tall
faults: Weight swinging away from the body
exercises.joint_notes: Wrists, shoulders and low back need to be healthy. Barbell versions: Teams G4 only. Not for osteoporosis without careful progression.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
exercises.progress_by: Pull → hang version → from the floor; DB → KB → barbell
exercises.regress_by: Pull only (no catch), KB swing, med ball scoop toss, landmine clean

exercises.name: Band Assisted Pull Up
exercises.pattern: Vertical pull: pull up / chin up / hangs
exercises.muscles: Lats, upper back, biceps, grip, core
exercises.why: The ultimate upper body bodyweight strength test. Hangs build grip (a strong predictor of longevity) and decompress the spine; negatives and isometrics build strength for the first pull up. LIFTMOR used jumping chin ups with drop landings for bone.
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
cues: Grip slightly wider than shoulders (chin up: palms facing you)
Pull the shoulder blades down first, then drive the elbows to the ribs
Chin over the bar, lower slowly to straight arms
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder pain: neutral grip, band assistance. Hanging can irritate some shoulders: build up gradually.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 or total reps
exercises.progress_by: Band assisted → negatives → bodyweight → weighted
exercises.regress_by: Lat pulldown, TRX assisted pull up, scapula pull up, dead hang

exercises.name: Swiss Ball DB Pullover
exercises.why: Pulldowns train the pull up pattern at any load, essential for members who can't yet do pull ups. Straight arm pulldowns and pullovers isolate the lats, which also helps overhead mobility.
variation_notes: Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
cues: Lean back slightly, chest up
Pull the shoulder blades down then the elbows to the ribs
Return slowly to a full stretch
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder friendly with neutral grip. Behind the neck versions: avoid for 40+.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, single arm, tempo, progress to band assisted pull ups
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, band pulldown, kneeling

exercises.muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip

Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. exercises.name: High to Low Cable Row

exercises.why: Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. exercises.name: TRX Pull Up Assisted Squat
exercises.why: Holding the TRX lets people counterbalance, so they can sit deeper and more upright than they could alone. It is the go to G1 squat for beginners, seniors, heavy members and anyone with knee or hip pain, and it builds confidence fast.
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
cues: Hold the handles at chest height with arms straight
Sit back and down, letting the straps take a little weight
Use the legs to stand, the arms only steady you
faults: Pulling with the arms to stand up
Leaning back so far the feet slide
Squatting deeper than the pain free range
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly. Ideal first squat after injury or replacement surgery (within surgeon's limits).
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0
exercises.progress_by: Use the straps less, slower tempo, add a pause, progress to goblet box squat
exercises.regress_by: Squat to a high box with the TRX, reduce depth

exercises.name: Inverted Row to Pull Up Progression
exercises.muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, core
exercises.why: Pulling your own bodyweight in a plank position. The angle sets the difficulty, so it scales from total beginner (standing upright) to advanced (feet elevated) in the same station. A core Optimal group exercise and part of Ed's screening (TRX row at 45 degrees).
variation_notes: Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.

exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder friendly. Neutral grip TRX handles are easiest on elbows.

exercises.name: KB High Pull (Single Arm)
exercises.muscles: Whole body: glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders
exercises.why: Explosive triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) trains power and rate of force development. Power declines faster than strength with age, so it must be trained, but the skill demand is high. DB, KB and landmine versions are far easier to learn and safer for groups than barbell versions.
variation_notes: One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.

Explode up through the legs and hips, shrug and pull the elbows high
Catch softly in a strong rack position (or overhead), stand tall
faults: Weight swinging away from the body

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge (Bodyweight)
exercises.why: Most training is forwards and backwards; lateral lunges train the side to side plane, building adductor strength and hip mobility that protect against groin strains and help golf, tennis and walking on uneven ground. Cossack squats are a great mobility and strength hybrid (Squat University and DeFranco's Limber 11).
cues: Step wide to the side, toes forward or slightly out
Sit back into one hip, keeping the other leg straight
Push back to the start through the bent leg
faults: Knee caving on the bent leg
Rounding the back to get lower
exercises.joint_notes: Groin and hip sensitive members: reduce range. Assisted versions (holding the rig) for seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
exercises.progress_by: Add load (goblet, DB, landmine), slider, deeper cossack
exercises.regress_by: Shorter range, hand support, lateral lunge rock (mobility)

exercises.name: Lateral Hop (Single Leg)
exercises.muscles: Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
exercises.why: Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
cues: Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes
Stick the landing for a second before the next rep
Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops
faults: Landing stiff legged or with knees caving
Too many reps (plyos are not cardio)
exercises.joint_notes: IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops; 2 to 3 sessions/week max, low total contacts (20 to 60)
exercises.progress_by: Landings → small jumps → box jumps → broad jumps → single leg hops → depth jumps
exercises.regress_by: Snap downs/drop squat and stick, step ups, sled push, med ball throws
exercises.group_alternative: Group swap (no jumping): sled push, fast step ups, med ball chest pass or slam, KB swing, fast sit to stand

exercises.name: Sled Lateral Drag
exercises.pattern: Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
exercises.why: The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
cues: Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet
Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes)
Keep steady steps and a neutral spine
faults: Hips too high or too low
Taking huge steps that slow the sled
exercises.joint_notes: Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
exercises.prescription: 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
exercises.progress_by: More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, slower, shorter distance

Cossack squats are a great mobility and strength hybrid (Squat University and DeFranco's Limber 11).
variation_notes: Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
cues: Step wide to the side, toes forward or slightly out
Sit back into one hip, keeping the other leg straight
Push back to the start through the bent leg
faults: Knee caving on the bent leg
Rounding the back to get lower
exercises.joint_notes: Groin and hip sensitive members: reduce range. Assisted versions (holding the rig) for seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
exercises.progress_by: Add load (goblet, DB, landmine), slider, deeper cossack
exercises.regress_by: Shorter range, hand support, lateral lunge rock (mobility)

exercises.name: Side Step Over Hurdles
exercises.why: Lateral step ups train single leg strength in the frontal plane, great for knee control and balance.
cues: Side on to the box, foot fully on
Drive up through the box leg
Lower with control
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly at low heights.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 each side
exercises.progress_by: Higher box, add load, knee drive
exercises.regress_by: Lower box, hand support

exercises.name: Curtsy Lunge (DB)
exercises.why: Stepping back and across challenges the hips in a different plane, hitting the side glutes and inner thighs. Good variety and good for hip stability and golf.
cues: Step one foot back and across behind the other
Lower straight down with the front knee tracking the toes
Push through the front foot to return
faults: Losing balance from too narrow a step
exercises.joint_notes: Can irritate knees and hips if the range is forced. Keep it pain free.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
exercises.progress_by: Add load, deficit, pair with a single leg RDL
exercises.regress_by: Shorter range, hand support, reverse lunge

exercises.name: Lateral Plank Walk
exercises.why: The plank trains the core to resist extension. Useful foundation, part of the Optimal screen (30s kneeling → full plank → plank with full tension). Long lever and RKC versions dramatically increase difficulty without longer holds.
cues: Elbows under shoulders, straight line head to heels
Squeeze glutes, pull the ribs down, push the floor away
Breathe, hold with full tension
faults: Holding for minutes with poor form
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder or wrist pain: dead bug or Pallof press instead. Prefer 20 to 30s high tension holds over long sloppy ones.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 20 to 40s (high tension)
exercises.progress_by: Long lever, RKC plank, leg lift, body saw
exercises.regress_by: Plank on knees, incline plank on a bench

exercises.name: Lateral Step Up (DB)
exercises.why: A real life movement (stairs, kerbs, climbing). Very back friendly, easy to scale by box height, and the concentric emphasis means little soreness. Knee drive and crossover versions add balance and hip work.
cues: Whole foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot
Lean forward slightly and drive through the box leg to stand tall
Step down with control, don't push off the bottom leg
faults: Box too high so the hip hikes
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly at lower heights. Use a low box and hand support for seniors and knee pain. Faster 'step ups' in BURN keep impact low.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Higher box, add DBs/goblet/barbell, add a knee drive, slower lowering
exercises.regress_by: Lower box, hand support, bodyweight

progress_to.name: Step Up to Single Leg RDL

exercises.name: Lateral Bear Crawl
exercises.why: Bear holds and crawls train the core and shoulders together and build coordination (Gambetta, Chek). Getting down to and moving on the floor is also a longevity skill.
cues: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, knees hover 2 to 3cm
Back flat, move opposite hand and foot together
Small steps, keep the hips still
exercises.joint_notes: Wrist pain: use fists or DB handles.
exercises.prescription: 3 x 20 to 40s or 10 to 20m
exercises.progress_by: Longer, add drag/load, reverse and lateral
exercises.regress_by: Static bear hold, knees down

exercises.name: Lateral Step Down
exercises.why: Controlled lowering from a step builds knee control and eccentric quad strength, the exact quality needed for walking downstairs. Also a key screening test for knee valgus and hip control.
cues: Stand on a box, other leg hanging off the front or side
Lower slowly by bending the standing knee, hips back slightly
Tap the heel lightly and return without pushing off the floor
faults: Hip dropping on the free side
exercises.joint_notes: Excellent for knee rehab when the box is low. Raise the height as control improves.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 each leg, 3s lowering
exercises.progress_by: Higher box, hold weight, slower lowering
exercises.regress_by: Lower box, hand support, Poliquin step up

exercises.name: Lateral Crab Walk (Hands and Feet)
