exercises.name: Lateral Med Ball Throw
exercises.pattern: Power: medicine ball throws and slams
exercises.muscles: Whole body power, rotational core (rotational throws), shoulders
exercises.why: Med ball throws are the safest way to train power for 40+ members: no catching heavy loads, no landing impact, and you can throw as hard as possible. Rotational throws (scoop toss, shot put) are THE golf power exercise (Gambetta, Chek). Wall balls combine a squat with a throw for conditioning.
cues: Load the hips (or rotate back through the hips for rotational throws)
Explode from the ground up: legs, hips, then arms
Throw with intent every rep, reset between reps
faults: Doing so many reps that it becomes slow cardio
exercises.joint_notes: Low impact and joint friendly. Use a soft ball for slams. Rotational throws: avoid with acute back pain. Wall balls need shoulder overhead range.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops (each side for rotational)
exercises.progress_by: Heavier ball, more distance/speed, step into the throw, single leg stance
exercises.regress_by: Lighter ball, half kneeling throw, slower controlled chops

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walk
exercises.muscles: Glute medius and minimus, hip stabilisers
exercises.why: The side glutes stop the knee caving and the pelvis dropping when on one leg. Weak glute meds are linked to knee pain, hip pain and back pain. Simple band work fixes it and works brilliantly as a warm up (Squat University, Boyle).
cues: Athletic stance, band around the knees or ankles
Push the knees out, step sideways (or lift the leg) leading with the heel
Stay low and keep the pelvis level
faults: Rocking the torso side to side
Letting the band pull the knees in
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly, ideal for hip and knee rehab.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each side
exercises.progress_by: Heavier band, band lower on the leg, side plank abduction
exercises.regress_by: Side lying with no band, smaller range

exercises.name: Side Lying Hip Adduction
exercises.why: Copenhagen planks are among the best researched ways to prevent groin injury, and adductor strength supports knee and hip health. Ball squeezes are a gentle entry point.
cues: Side plank with the top leg on a bench (inside of the knee for short lever, ankle for long lever)
Lift the hips into a straight line by squeezing the top leg down
Hold or lift and lower
exercises.joint_notes: Short lever first. Groin pain: ball squeeze isometrics.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 15 to 30s each side
exercises.progress_by: Short → long lever, add leg raises
exercises.regress_by: Ball squeeze, side lying adduction

exercises.name: Lateral Sled Pull
exercises.pattern: Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
exercises.why: The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
cues: Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet
Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes)
Keep steady steps and a neutral spine
faults: Hips too high or too low
Taking huge steps that slow the sled
exercises.joint_notes: Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
exercises.prescription: 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
exercises.progress_by: More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, slower, shorter distance

Hold or lift and lower
exercises.joint_notes: Short lever first. Groin pain: ball squeeze isometrics.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 15 to 30s each side
exercises.progress_by: Short → long lever, add leg raises
exercises.regress_by: Ball squeeze, side lying adduction

exercises.name: Shuffle and Sprint
exercises.why: Change of direction, rhythm and footwork. Builds coordination and reaction (Gambetta), useful for sport and falls prevention, but most variations involve running or hopping.
variation_notes: Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
cues: Stay low and light on the feet
Short quick steps, eyes up
Control each change of direction
exercises.joint_notes: IMPACT (running/hopping): excluded from group sessions. Teams only after screening.
exercises.prescription: 4 to 8 x 10 to 20s, full recovery
exercises.progress_by: Faster, more complex patterns
exercises.regress_by: Walking footwork patterns, lateral band walk, sled lateral drag

exercises.name: Lateral Plyo Step
exercises.muscles: Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
exercises.why: Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
cues: Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes
Stick the landing for a second before the next rep
Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops
faults: Landing stiff legged or with knees caving
Too many reps (plyos are not cardio)
exercises.joint_notes: IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops; 2 to 3 sessions/week max, low total contacts (20 to 60)
exercises.progress_by: Landings → small jumps → box jumps → broad jumps → single leg hops → depth jumps
exercises.regress_by: Snap downs/drop squat and stick, step ups, sled push, med ball throws
exercises.group_alternative: Group swap (no jumping): sled push, fast step ups, med ball chest pass or slam, KB swing, fast sit to stand

exercises.name: Banded Standing Hip Abduction
exercises.muscles: Glute medius and minimus, hip stabilisers
exercises.why: The side glutes stop the knee caving and the pelvis dropping when on one leg. Weak glute meds are linked to knee pain, hip pain and back pain. Simple band work fixes it and works brilliantly as a warm up (Squat University, Boyle).
variation_notes: Band resistance gets harder at the top (accommodating resistance) and can cue better positions such as knees out.
cues: Athletic stance, band around the knees or ankles
Push the knees out, step sideways (or lift the leg) leading with the heel
Stay low and keep the pelvis level
faults: Rocking the torso side to side
Letting the band pull the knees in
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly, ideal for hip and knee rehab.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each side
exercises.progress_by: Heavier band, band lower on the leg, side plank abduction

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.muscles: Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
exercises.why: Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
cues: Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes
Stick the landing for a second before the next rep
Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops
faults: Landing stiff legged or with knees caving
Too many reps (plyos are not cardio)
exercises.joint_notes: IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.

exercises.regress_by: Snap downs/drop squat and stick, step ups, sled push, med ball throws

exercises.name: Pallof Press (Cable)
exercises.why: The core's main job is to stop unwanted movement. The Pallof press resists the cable pulling you round, training the anti rotation strength that protects the back and transfers force in golf, tennis and lifting (McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove).
variation_notes: Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
cues: Side on to the cable at chest height, brace
Press the handle straight out from the chest and hold 2s
Don't let the hands or hips rotate, return to the chest
exercises.joint_notes: Excellent for back pain. Half kneeling reduces hip involvement and isolates the core.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
exercises.progress_by: Tall kneeling → half kneeling → split → standing → walkouts, add overhead reach, heavier
exercises.regress_by: Lighter band, closer to the anchor, iso hold

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Tap

cues: Elbows under shoulders, straight line head to heels
Squeeze glutes, pull the ribs down, push the floor away
Breathe, hold with full tension
faults: Holding for minutes with poor form
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder or wrist pain: dead bug or Pallof press instead. Prefer 20 to 30s high tension holds over long sloppy ones.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 20 to 40s (high tension)
exercises.progress_by: Long lever, RKC plank, leg lift, body saw
exercises.regress_by: Plank on knees, incline plank on a bench

variation_notes: Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
cues: Feet stable, brace
Pull the cable diagonally across the body, letting the hips and upper back turn together
Control the return
faults: Twisting only at the low back
exercises.joint_notes: Keep rotation through the hips and upper back, not the lumbar spine. Half kneeling is most back friendly.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
exercises.progress_by: Standing, heavier, with a step, faster (power)
exercises.regress_by: Half/tall kneeling, lighter, smaller range

exercises.name: Single Arm KB Swing (Anti Rotation)
exercises.muscles: Glutes, hamstrings, core, grip, cardiovascular system
exercises.why: The king of hinge conditioning (Dan John, Pavel). Trains explosive hip extension (power) and heart rate at the same time with no impact on the knees. Excellent for fat loss, posture and glute strength. Dead stop versions teach control; single arm versions add anti rotation.
variation_notes: One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
cues: Hike the bell back high between the thighs
Snap the hips forward, squeeze the glutes, let the bell float to chest height
Let it fall, hinge late, keep the spine neutral
faults: Squatting the swing instead of hinging
exercises.joint_notes: Back friendly when the hinge is good. Teach the KB deadlift first. Not for acute low back pain. American (overhead) swings stress shoulders and low back: use hip height swings instead.
exercises.prescription: 4 to 10 sets x 10 to 20 reps, or EMOM; 'hike, snap, float'
exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, single arm, alternating, swings EMOM, heavier with fewer reps for power
exercises.regress_by: KB deadlift, dead stop swing, lighter bell, cable pull through
same_level_swaps: Single Arm KB Swing to Catch

exercises.name: Single Arm Cable Row with Rotation
exercises.muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
exercises.why: Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
variation_notes: One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
cues: Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow
Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back)
Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch
exercises.joint_notes: Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps
exercises.regress_by: Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row
same_level_swaps: Split Stance Single Arm Cable Row

exercises.name: Rotational Press (Landmine)
exercises.why: The landmine press moves on an arc between a horizontal and vertical press, letting the shoulder blade move freely. It is the most shoulder friendly way to press overhead and the go to for members who can't press straight overhead (Cressey). Half kneeling adds core and hip stability.
variation_notes: Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn.
cues: Hold the end of the bar at the shoulder, ribs down, glutes tight
Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around
Lower with control back to the shoulder
exercises.joint_notes: Best press for shoulder pain and limited overhead range.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each arm)
exercises.progress_by: Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, two hands, half kneeling

exercises.name: T Rotation Press Up
exercises.muscles: Chest, shoulders, triceps, serratus, core (anti extension)
exercises.why: A moving plank: chest and arm strength plus core control. The shoulder blades move freely, which is healthier for shoulders than bench pressing. Easy to scale by hand height so every level in a group can do the same exercise. Push up plus adds serratus work for shoulder health.
cues: Hands just outside shoulders, body in a straight line, glutes and abs tight
Lower the chest between the hands, elbows about 45 degrees from the body
Push the floor away until arms are straight and the upper back is spread
exercises.joint_notes: Wrist pain: use DB handles or fists. Shoulder pain: elevate the hands and keep elbows tucked.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 6 to 15 reps (or total reps progression)
exercises.progress_by: Lower the hand height (wall → bench → box → floor), tempo, pause, feet elevated, add a weighted vest/plate
exercises.regress_by: Higher incline (bench or wall), knee push up, shorter range

exercises.name: Open Book (Side Lying)
exercises.muscles: Thoracic spine rotation and extension, lats, pecs
exercises.why: The upper back should move; the low back should be stable (joint by joint). Stiff upper backs cause rounded posture, shoulder pain and low back pain, and limit the golf swing. Daily T spine drills fix it.
cues: Keep the hips still (knee pinned or in quadruped)
Rotate/extend through the upper back, follow the hand with the eyes
Breathe out into the end range
exercises.joint_notes: Very safe. Osteoporosis: avoid forced flexion; gentle rotation and extension are fine.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Add a reach, hold end range longer
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range, seated version

exercises.name: Russian Twist (Plate)
exercises.why: Popular rotation exercises that combine spinal flexion and twisting. They do train the obliques, but the combination of flexion and rotation is the riskiest for discs.
cues: Sit tall, lean back slightly
Rotate from the ribcage, not just the arms
Control every rep
exercises.joint_notes: AVOID for back pain, disc history and osteoporosis (McGill). Prefer Pallof press and chops.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
exercises.progress_by: Feet up, heavier
exercises.regress_by: Feet down, no load, Pallof press instead

exercises.name: Russian Twist (Med Ball)
exercises.pattern: Power: medicine ball throws and slams
exercises.muscles: Whole body power, rotational core (rotational throws), shoulders
exercises.why: Med ball throws are the safest way to train power for 40+ members: no catching heavy loads, no landing impact, and you can throw as hard as possible. Rotational throws (scoop toss, shot put) are THE golf power exercise (Gambetta, Chek). Wall balls combine a squat with a throw for conditioning.
cues: Load the hips (or rotate back through the hips for rotational throws)
Explode from the ground up: legs, hips, then arms
Throw with intent every rep, reset between reps
faults: Doing so many reps that it becomes slow cardio
exercises.joint_notes: Low impact and joint friendly. Use a soft ball for slams. Rotational throws: avoid with acute back pain. Wall balls need shoulder overhead range.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops (each side for rotational)
exercises.progress_by: Heavier ball, more distance/speed, step into the throw, single leg stance
exercises.regress_by: Lighter ball, half kneeling throw, slower controlled chops

Draw small circles with the elbows
Keep the hips and back still

exercises.name: Suitcase Deadlift (Anti Lateral Flexion)
exercises.why: The safest way to teach lifting from the floor. Picking things up is a life skill (Primal Pattern 'bend'). Raising the bell on blocks reduces range for beginners and back pain; suitcase versions add anti lateral flexion.
variation_notes: One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
cues: Bell between the feet (or beside for suitcase), hinge down with a flat back
Grip, pull the shoulders down, brace
Push the floor away and stand tall, squeeze the glutes
exercises.joint_notes: Very back friendly. Elevate the bell on a step for limited hip mobility or back history.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, double KB, lower to the floor, progress to RDL, swing and trap bar
exercises.regress_by: Bell on a block/step, hinge drill

cues: Weight tight to the chest
Stand tall, ribs down, walk slowly
Breathe behind the brace

cues: Athletic stance, brace
Drive the waves from the shoulders and hips
Keep a steady rhythm
exercises.joint_notes: Low impact. Rope jumping jacks involve jumping: swap to step jacks in groups.
exercises.prescription: 6 to 10 x 20 to 30s / 30 to 60s rest
exercises.progress_by: Longer, faster, heavier rope
exercises.regress_by: Shorter intervals, kneeling

exercises.name: Rotational Lunge (Med Ball)
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance, grip when loaded
exercises.why: Forward and walking lunges add deceleration and balance: you have to control the body moving forward over the front leg. Very functional and very metabolic, so they suit BURN and HYBRID sessions. Loaded carry lunges add grip and core.
cues: Long step forward, land heel first
Drop the back knee down, front knee over the middle of the foot

Keep the weight stacked over the shoulder

exercises.name: Bird Dog Hold
exercises.pattern: Core: anti rotation / anti extension (bird dog)
exercises.muscles: Spinal extensors, glutes, deep core, shoulder stabilisers
exercises.why: Part of the McGill Big 3. Reaching the opposite arm and leg while keeping the spine still trains the back extensors and anti rotation control with very low spinal load. A safe daily exercise for back pain and the foundation of Paul Chek's horse stance progressions.
variation_notes: Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.

Reach the opposite arm and leg long (not high), hold 8 to 10s
Sweep back under without the hips rotating

exercises.regress_by: Arm only or leg only

Roll or slide out only as far as you can keep the back flat
Pull back using the abs and lats

exercises.progress_by: Longer range, from feet
exercises.regress_by: Swiss ball rollout short range, plank

Brace and lift the head and shoulders slightly as one unit
Hold 8 to 10s, lower
exercises.joint_notes: Back pain friendly. Part of the Big 3.
exercises.prescription: Descending pyramid: 6, 4, 2 reps with 8 to 10s holds
exercises.progress_by: Raise elbows off the floor, longer holds
exercises.regress_by: Shorter holds
same_level_swaps: McGill Big 3 (Curl Up, Side Plank, Bird Dog)

No twisting

exercises.why: Copenhagen planks are among the best researched ways to prevent groin injury, and adductor strength supports knee and hip health. Ball squeezes are a gentle entry point.

Lift the hips into a straight line by squeezing the top leg down
Hold or lift and lower

exercises.progress_by: Short → long lever, add leg raises
exercises.regress_by: Ball squeeze, side lying adduction

Drive one knee towards the chest at a time
Keep the hips level

exercises.progress_by: Faster, sliders, cross body
exercises.regress_by: Hands on a bench, slow

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilt

Breathe in through the nose expanding 360 degrees (belly, sides, back)
Exhale slowly fully, feeling the ribs drop

exercises.prescription: 5 to 10 slow breaths
exercises.progress_by: Add movement (dead bug with breathing)
exercises.regress_by: Shorter sets

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry (DB)
exercises.why: Dan John says loaded carries change lives. Picking up heavy things and walking trains grip (a strong longevity predictor), posture, core and conditioning all at once, with low technical demand and low injury risk. Every member, every week.

Stand tall, shoulders down, walk with short controlled steps
Breathe and keep the ribs down
faults: Leaning forward or side to side
exercises.joint_notes: Very safe. Pick up and put down with a good hinge. Grip limited members: straps are fine to train the rest.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, longer, on the toes, with steps/obstacles; Dan John standard: bodyweight total for men
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, shorter, static hold

exercises.regress_by: Lighter, single position

Stand tall, ribs down, walk slowly

exercises.name: Sled Push
exercises.pattern: Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
exercises.why: The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
cues: Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet
Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes)
Keep steady steps and a neutral spine
faults: Hips too high or too low
Taking huge steps that slow the sled
exercises.joint_notes: Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
exercises.prescription: 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
exercises.progress_by: More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, slower, shorter distance

cues: Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet
Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes)
Keep steady steps and a neutral spine
faults: Hips too high or too low
Taking huge steps that slow the sled
exercises.joint_notes: Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
exercises.prescription: 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
exercises.progress_by: More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, slower, shorter distance

exercises.name: Overhead Carry (Double KB)
exercises.why: Holding weight overhead while walking trains shoulder stability and core in one. Bottoms up holds make the rotator cuff work hard with light weight: brilliant for shoulder rehab.
variation_notes: Double KB: heavier total load plus a front rack or bilateral grip demand.
cues: Arm locked, biceps by the ear, shoulder packed
Ribs down, walk slowly
Keep the weight stacked over the shoulder
exercises.joint_notes: Needs pain free overhead range. Waiter's carry (arm at 90 degrees) is an easier option.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, double, bottoms up
exercises.regress_by: Waiter's carry, lighter, static hold

exercises.name: Dead Hang (Grip)
exercises.pattern: Vertical pull: pull up / chin up / hangs
exercises.muscles: Lats, upper back, biceps, grip, core
exercises.why: The ultimate upper body bodyweight strength test. Hangs build grip (a strong predictor of longevity) and decompress the spine; negatives and isometrics build strength for the first pull up. LIFTMOR used jumping chin ups with drop landings for bone.
cues: Grip slightly wider than shoulders (chin up: palms facing you)
Pull the shoulder blades down first, then drive the elbows to the ribs
Chin over the bar, lower slowly to straight arms
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder pain: neutral grip, band assistance. Hanging can irritate some shoulders: build up gradually.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 or total reps
exercises.progress_by: Band assisted → negatives → bodyweight → weighted
exercises.regress_by: Lat pulldown, TRX assisted pull up, scapula pull up, dead hang

exercises.name: Farmer's Walk Lunge
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, hamstrings, balance, grip when loaded
exercises.why: Forward and walking lunges add deceleration and balance: you have to control the body moving forward over the front leg. Very functional and very metabolic, so they suit BURN and HYBRID sessions. Loaded carry lunges add grip and core.
cues: Long step forward, land heel first
Drop the back knee down, front knee over the middle of the foot
Push through the front foot and step through to the next rep
faults: Short choppy steps that load the front knee
exercises.joint_notes: More knee stress than reverse lunges. Swap to reverse lunges or split squats with knee pain. Needs space in groups.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg) or 20 to 30m
exercises.progress_by: Add load (DB, KB rack, overhead), pulses, longer distance
exercises.regress_by: Reverse lunge, split squat, hand support

exercises.name: Pogo Hops

cues: Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes
Stick the landing for a second before the next rep
Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops
faults: Landing stiff legged or with knees caving
Too many reps (plyos are not cardio)

exercises.name: Landmine Squat to Press (Power)
exercises.why: Links a squat and an overhead press into one total body movement. Very metabolic, great for BURN and HYBRID sessions, and the legs help drive the weight overhead so people can press more.
variation_notes: Landmine: the arc path is shoulder and back friendly and very easy to learn.
Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
cues: Squat with the weight in the rack
Drive up hard and use that momentum to press overhead
Lock out with biceps by the ears, ribs down, then lower back to the rack
faults: Pressing before the legs finish the drive
Arching the low back at the top
Losing the rack position and squatting with the elbows dropped
exercises.joint_notes: Needs pain free overhead range. With shoulder pain swap to squat to landmine press. Watch technique as fatigue builds in circuits.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 8 to 12 reps, or 30 to 40s in circuits
exercises.progress_by: Add load, double KBs, barbell, more rounds or density
exercises.regress_by: Goblet squat to press, landmine squat to press, split into separate squat and press

exercises.name: Med Ball Chest Pass
exercises.pattern: Power: medicine ball throws and slams
exercises.muscles: Whole body power, rotational core (rotational throws), shoulders
exercises.why: Med ball throws are the safest way to train power for 40+ members: no catching heavy loads, no landing impact, and you can throw as hard as possible. Rotational throws (scoop toss, shot put) are THE golf power exercise (Gambetta, Chek). Wall balls combine a squat with a throw for conditioning.
cues: Load the hips (or rotate back through the hips for rotational throws)
Explode from the ground up: legs, hips, then arms
Throw with intent every rep, reset between reps
faults: Doing so many reps that it becomes slow cardio
exercises.joint_notes: Low impact and joint friendly. Use a soft ball for slams. Rotational throws: avoid with acute back pain. Wall balls need shoulder overhead range.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops (each side for rotational)
exercises.progress_by: Heavier ball, more distance/speed, step into the throw, single leg stance
exercises.regress_by: Lighter ball, half kneeling throw, slower controlled chops

exercises.why: Med ball throws are the safest way to train power for 40+ members: no catching heavy loads, no landing impact, and you can throw as hard as possible. Rotational throws (scoop toss, shot put) are THE golf power exercise (Gambetta, Chek). Wall balls combine a squat with a throw for conditioning.
cues: Load the hips (or rotate back through the hips for rotational throws)
Explode from the ground up: legs, hips, then arms
Throw with intent every rep, reset between reps
faults: Doing so many reps that it becomes slow cardio
exercises.joint_notes: Low impact and joint friendly. Use a soft ball for slams. Rotational throws: avoid with acute back pain. Wall balls need shoulder overhead range.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops (each side for rotational)
exercises.progress_by: Heavier ball, more distance/speed, step into the throw, single leg stance
exercises.regress_by: Lighter ball, half kneeling throw, slower controlled chops

exercises.name: Single Leg Hop
exercises.muscles: Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
exercises.why: Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
cues: Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes
Stick the landing for a second before the next rep
Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops
faults: Landing stiff legged or with knees caving
Too many reps (plyos are not cardio)
exercises.joint_notes: IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops; 2 to 3 sessions/week max, low total contacts (20 to 60)
exercises.progress_by: Landings → small jumps → box jumps → broad jumps → single leg hops → depth jumps
exercises.regress_by: Snap downs/drop squat and stick, step ups, sled push, med ball throws
exercises.group_alternative: Group swap (no jumping): sled push, fast step ups, med ball chest pass or slam, KB swing, fast sit to stand

Land softly with bent elbows
Reset each rep

exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops
exercises.progress_by: Higher, then clap
exercises.regress_by: Incline plyo push up, med ball chest pass
exercises.group_alternative: Group swap: med ball chest pass or explosive band press

cues: Light on the toes
Rhythm
Soft knees

exercises.progress_by: Faster, longer
exercises.regress_by: Step jacks
exercises.group_alternative: Group swap: step jacks, marching, assault bike

exercises.name: Explosive Band Row
exercises.muscles: Upper back, lats, rear shoulders, biceps, grip
exercises.why: Rows build the upper back that holds posture upright and balances pressing. Chest supported rows remove the low back from the equation; single arm rows allow heavier loading and fix imbalances; bent over rows add hinge endurance. Aim for about 2 pulls for every push in desk based members.
cues: Brace, shoulder blade pulls first, then the elbow
Row towards the hip (lats) or lower ribs (upper back)
Pause, lower slowly to a full stretch
exercises.joint_notes: Chest supported and cable versions are the most back friendly. Bent over versions load the low back: avoid pairing with RDLs for 40+.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, pause at the top, tempo, single arm, 1.5 reps
exercises.regress_by: Chest supported row, cable row, TRX row

exercises.name: Sled Sprint (Push)
exercises.pattern: Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
exercises.why: The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
variation_notes: Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
cues: Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet
Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes)
Keep steady steps and a neutral spine
faults: Hips too high or too low
Taking huge steps that slow the sled
exercises.joint_notes: Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
exercises.prescription: 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
exercises.progress_by: More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, slower, shorter distance

exercises.name: Sled Pull
exercises.pattern: Carry / gait: sled push, pull and drag
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, calves, whole body conditioning
exercises.why: The sled is the most joint friendly strength and conditioning tool in the gym: concentric only, so almost no soreness, no impact and no technique to fail. Ben Patrick uses backward drags for knee health; DeFranco uses pushes for conditioning. Every member at every level can use it.
cues: Push: arms extended or bent, body at 45 degrees, drive through the balls of the feet
Drag backward: lean back, small steps, push through the front of the foot (knees over toes)
Keep steady steps and a neutral spine
faults: Hips too high or too low
Taking huge steps that slow the sled
exercises.joint_notes: Almost universally safe. Backward drag is a knee pain staple. Heavy pushes raise blood pressure: keep breathing.
exercises.prescription: 6 to 10 x 15 to 25m, walk back recovery; or 3 to 5 min backward drag in warm up
exercises.progress_by: More weight, faster (sprints), longer distance, less rest
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, slower, shorter distance

exercises.name: Sled Drag Backwards
exercises.why: Ben Patrick's number one knee tool: walking backwards loads the quads with the knee travelling over the toes, floods the knee with blood and is nearly impossible to overdo.
cues: Lean back slightly against the sled (or hold the treadmill rails)
Small steps, push through the front of the foot
Knees travel over the toes
exercises.joint_notes: Knee pain staple. Very safe.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 min warm up, or 4 to 6 x 20m
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, longer
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, treadmill flat

exercises.name: Box Step Ups (Fast)

variation_notes: Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
cues: Whole foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot
Lean forward slightly and drive through the box leg to stand tall
Step down with control, don't push off the bottom leg
faults: Box too high so the hip hikes
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly at lower heights. Use a low box and hand support for seniors and knee pain. Faster 'step ups' in BURN keep impact low.

Walk slowly without leaning towards or away from the weight
Swap hands
exercises.joint_notes: Back pain friendly.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s each side
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, march with high knees, longer
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, static hold

Move through each step slowly: roll to elbow, hand, high bridge, sweep the leg, kneel, stand
Reverse every step with control

exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 reps each side, slow
exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, full get up
exercises.regress_by: Half get up, shoe on the fist, no weight

exercises.name: Isometric External Rotation

Push into the wall/band gently and build to about 70%
Hold 30 to 45s, breathe
exercises.joint_notes: Rehab friendly.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 45s holds, rest 60s, about 70% effort
exercises.progress_by: Longer holds, harder push, move to band rotations
exercises.regress_by: Lighter push

Press up and forward, letting the shoulder blade reach around

exercises.progress_by: Half kneeling → tall kneeling → split stance → standing → push press; add plates
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, two hands, half kneeling

cues: Keep the hips still (knee pinned or in quadruped)
Rotate/extend through the upper back, follow the hand with the eyes
Breathe out into the end range

exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Add a reach, hold end range longer
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range, seated version

exercises.name: Face Pull with External Rotation
exercises.muscles: Rear shoulders, rotator cuff (external rotators), mid traps
exercises.why: Face pulls combine a high row with external rotation, strengthening the muscles that keep shoulders healthy and posture upright. Cressey and DeFranco use them in almost every programme to balance all the pressing. Optimal: at least 2x per week for desk workers.
cues: Rope at forehead height, thumbs pointing back
Pull towards the face, elbows high, separate the rope
Finish with the knuckles beside the ears (like a double bicep pose), pause
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder friendly and often therapeutic.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 12 to 20 reps, pause 1s
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, slower, add external rotation emphasis
exercises.regress_by: Band face pull, lighter

Move the joint through its biggest circle slowly
Keep tension the whole way
exercises.joint_notes: Universally safe.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 slow reps each direction
exercises.progress_by: Bigger circle, more tension
exercises.regress_by: Smaller circle

Return slowly

exercises.name: Hanging (Supported)
exercises.pattern: Vertical pull: pull up / chin up / hangs
exercises.muscles: Lats, upper back, biceps, grip, core
exercises.why: The ultimate upper body bodyweight strength test. Hangs build grip (a strong predictor of longevity) and decompress the spine; negatives and isometrics build strength for the first pull up. LIFTMOR used jumping chin ups with drop landings for bone.
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
cues: Grip slightly wider than shoulders (chin up: palms facing you)
Pull the shoulder blades down first, then drive the elbows to the ribs
Chin over the bar, lower slowly to straight arms
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder pain: neutral grip, band assistance. Hanging can irritate some shoulders: build up gradually.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 or total reps
exercises.progress_by: Band assisted → negatives → bodyweight → weighted
exercises.regress_by: Lat pulldown, TRX assisted pull up, scapula pull up, dead hang

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Light, Full Range)
exercises.why: Pulldowns train the pull up pattern at any load, essential for members who can't yet do pull ups. Straight arm pulldowns and pullovers isolate the lats, which also helps overhead mobility.
variation_notes: Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Lean back slightly, chest up
Pull the shoulder blades down then the elbows to the ribs
Return slowly to a full stretch
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder friendly with neutral grip. Behind the neck versions: avoid for 40+.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, single arm, tempo, progress to band assisted pull ups
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, band pulldown, kneeling

exercises.name: Scapula Retraction (TRX)
exercises.muscles: Mid and lower traps, rhomboids, lats
exercises.why: Training the shoulder blade to move (down, back, up) before the arm pulls. Scapula pull ups and retractions are the first step towards rows and pull ups (G1 of the Optimal row screen).
cues: Arms straight
Move only the shoulder blades
Pause and return
exercises.joint_notes: Rehab friendly.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
exercises.progress_by: Full rows/pull ups
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range

exercises.name: Waiter's Carry (Light)
exercises.why: Holding weight overhead while walking trains shoulder stability and core in one. Bottoms up holds make the rotator cuff work hard with light weight: brilliant for shoulder rehab.
variation_notes: Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Arm locked, biceps by the ear, shoulder packed
Ribs down, walk slowly
Keep the weight stacked over the shoulder
exercises.joint_notes: Needs pain free overhead range. Waiter's carry (arm at 90 degrees) is an easier option.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, double, bottoms up
exercises.regress_by: Waiter's carry, lighter, static hold

exercises.name: Single Leg Balance (Eyes Closed)
exercises.muscles: Foot, ankle, hip stabilisers, nervous system
exercises.why: Balance falls away quickly with age and inactivity; falls are a leading cause of injury in older adults. Single leg balance is part of the Optimal screen. Train it every session for 60+ (Gambetta: postural alignment and dynamic balance are the foundation).
cues: Stand tall near a support
Grip the floor with the foot, soft knee
Hold or reach while keeping the hips level
exercises.joint_notes: Always near a rail or rig for seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 x 20 to 30s each leg
exercises.progress_by: Eyes closed, cushion, reach, catch a ball
exercises.regress_by: Hand on support, tandem stance

exercises.name: Clam Shell
exercises.muscles: Glute medius and minimus, hip stabilisers
exercises.why: The side glutes stop the knee caving and the pelvis dropping when on one leg. Weak glute meds are linked to knee pain, hip pain and back pain. Simple band work fixes it and works brilliantly as a warm up (Squat University, Boyle).
cues: Athletic stance, band around the knees or ankles
Push the knees out, step sideways (or lift the leg) leading with the heel
Stay low and keep the pelvis level
faults: Rocking the torso side to side
Letting the band pull the knees in
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly, ideal for hip and knee rehab.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each side
exercises.progress_by: Heavier band, band lower on the leg, side plank abduction
exercises.regress_by: Side lying with no band, smaller range

exercises.name: Step Up (Low Box)
exercises.why: A real life movement (stairs, kerbs, climbing). Very back friendly, easy to scale by box height, and the concentric emphasis means little soreness. Knee drive and crossover versions add balance and hip work.
cues: Whole foot on the box, knee over the middle of the foot
Lean forward slightly and drive through the box leg to stand tall
Step down with control, don't push off the bottom leg
faults: Box too high so the hip hikes
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly at lower heights. Use a low box and hand support for seniors and knee pain. Faster 'step ups' in BURN keep impact low.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Higher box, add DBs/goblet/barbell, add a knee drive, slower lowering
exercises.regress_by: Lower box, hand support, bodyweight

progress_to.name: Step Up to Single Leg RDL

exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each side
exercises.progress_by: Heavier band, band lower on the leg, side plank abduction
exercises.regress_by: Side lying with no band, smaller range

exercises.name: Single Leg RDL (Supported)
exercises.muscles: Hamstrings, glutes (incl. glute med), foot and ankle stability
exercises.why: Single leg hinges build hamstring and glute strength, balance and hip stability one side at a time, and they spare the spine because loads are lighter. Kickstand and B stance versions give a stepping stone with the back foot for support. Hip airplanes train hip rotation control (great for golf).
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
cues: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, other leg reaching back
Hinge forward as one straight line from head to heel, hips square
Drive the standing heel into the floor and squeeze the glute to stand
faults: Hips opening up (rotating) towards the ceiling
Rounding the back to reach the floor
exercises.joint_notes: Back friendly. Balance limits load: use a support or kickstand first. Excellent for golfers and runners.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Kickstand → full single leg, add load (DB/KB, double KB, landmine), slower tempo, add a row or reach
exercises.regress_by: Supported single leg RDL (hand on rig), kickstand RDL, bodyweight

exercises.name: Split Squat (Supported)
exercises.why: The entry point of the single leg ladder. A static split stance gives a stable base, so people learn to load one leg at a time safely. It builds balance, fixes imbalances and is far easier on the back than heavy bilateral squats. Front foot elevated adds knee travel (ATG style); cable and landmine versions add stability.
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
cues: Long split stance, both feet pointing forward, hip width apart
Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor
Push through the front foot to stand, keep the torso tall
faults: Lunging forward instead of dropping down
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly when depth is controlled. Use a pad under the back knee. Hold a support for balance in seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Add load, elevate the front foot (ATG style), then elevate the back foot (RFESS)
exercises.regress_by: TRX or rig assisted split squat, shorter range, isometric split squat hold

exercises.name: Donkey Kick
exercises.why: Cable/band pull throughs teach the hip hinge with the load pulling from behind, so people naturally sit the hips back and finish with the glutes. Kickbacks and quadruped hip extensions isolate the glutes for activation and rehab.
cues: Face away from the cable, rope between the legs
Hinge back letting the rope pull the hips back
Drive the hips through and squeeze the glutes, stand tall
exercises.joint_notes: Very back friendly. A great swing and deadlift regression.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, pause at the top, progress to KB swing
exercises.regress_by: Band version, shorter range

exercises.name: Hip Flexor March (Supine)
exercises.why: Hip flexor strength (especially lifting the knee above 90 degrees) declines with age and affects walking, stairs and tripping. Ben Patrick includes it in ATG Zero.
cues: Sit or lie tall
Lift the knee up without leaning back
Lower slowly
exercises.joint_notes: Gentle and safe. Hip impingement: keep below pain.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
exercises.progress_by: Band resistance, standing, longer holds
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range

exercises.name: Hip Thrust (Paused)
exercises.why: Bridges and hip thrusts train the glutes at their strongest point (full hip extension) with almost no spinal load. They are essential for back pain, knee pain, posture, sprinting and golf power, and are safe for nearly everyone. Single leg versions fix imbalances.
variation_notes: Paused version: holding the hardest position removes the bounce and builds strength exactly where people usually fail.
cues: Feet flat, shins vertical at the top
Tuck the ribs down, drive through the heels and squeeze the glutes to lift
Pause at the top without arching the low back, lower slowly
faults: Arching the low back instead of extending the hips
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly. Use a pad on the hips when loaded. Shoulder elevated versions need a stable bench.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (pause 1 to 2s at the top)
exercises.progress_by: Bridge → hip thrust off a bench → load (DB, barbell) → single leg, add pauses or bands
exercises.regress_by: Floor bridge, shorter range, isometric hold

exercises.name: Banded Hip Flexor March
exercises.why: Hip flexor strength (especially lifting the knee above 90 degrees) declines with age and affects walking, stairs and tripping. Ben Patrick includes it in ATG Zero.
variation_notes: Band resistance gets harder at the top (accommodating resistance) and can cue better positions such as knees out.
cues: Sit or lie tall
Lift the knee up without leaning back
Lower slowly
exercises.joint_notes: Gentle and safe. Hip impingement: keep below pain.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
exercises.progress_by: Band resistance, standing, longer holds
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range

exercises.name: Couch Stretch
exercises.muscles: Target muscles and joints vary (named in the exercise)
exercises.why: Static and gentle mobility work restores range lost from sitting and ageing. Best used where a screen shows a restriction (Squat University: screen, correct, retest), and to cool down. McKenzie press ups and extension work often relieve disc type back pain; flexion stretches often suit stenosis type pain: individualise.
cues: Get into position slowly
Breathe out to relax into range, no bouncing
Hold 30 to 60s or do slow reps
faults: Stretching instead of strengthening when stability is the issue
exercises.joint_notes: Gentle and safe. Stop if symptoms travel down the leg. Osteoporosis: avoid loaded flexion stretches.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Longer holds, deeper range, add loaded stretching
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range, supported versions

exercises.name: Adductor Rock Back
exercises.why: Gentle spinal mobility for back care and warm ups. Extension drills (prone lying, McKenzie press ups) often ease disc type back pain; flexion drills (knee to chest, child's pose) often ease stiffness and stenosis type pain. Find the direction that helps the individual (McGill: find the pain triggers) and use it.
cues: Move slowly through comfortable range
Breathe out into the end range
Stop if symptoms travel down a leg
exercises.joint_notes: Generally very safe. Osteoporosis: avoid repeated or loaded spinal flexion. Pain spreading into a leg: stop and refer.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Bigger range, add breathing holds
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
exercises.why: Hip internal and external rotation are often the first ranges lost with age and are critical for the golf swing, squat depth and low back health (joint by joint).
cues: Sit tall in 90/90 or lie in position
Rotate through the hips, keep the chest tall
Move slowly, hold the end range
exercises.joint_notes: Hip pain: reduce range.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Hands free, hip lifts, longer holds
exercises.regress_by: Hands support

exercises.regress_by: Side lying with no band, smaller range

exercises.name: Glute Med Wall Press
exercises.muscles: Glute medius and minimus, hip stabilisers
exercises.why: The side glutes stop the knee caving and the pelvis dropping when on one leg. Weak glute meds are linked to knee pain, hip pain and back pain. Simple band work fixes it and works brilliantly as a warm up (Squat University, Boyle).
cues: Athletic stance, band around the knees or ankles
Push the knees out, step sideways (or lift the leg) leading with the heel
Stay low and keep the pelvis level
faults: Rocking the torso side to side
Letting the band pull the knees in
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly, ideal for hip and knee rehab.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each side
exercises.progress_by: Heavier band, band lower on the leg, side plank abduction
exercises.regress_by: Side lying with no band, smaller range

exercises.name: Isometric Adductor Squeeze (Ball)
exercises.why: Copenhagen planks are among the best researched ways to prevent groin injury, and adductor strength supports knee and hip health. Ball squeezes are a gentle entry point.
variation_notes: Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
cues: Side plank with the top leg on a bench (inside of the knee for short lever, ankle for long lever)
Lift the hips into a straight line by squeezing the top leg down
Hold or lift and lower
exercises.joint_notes: Short lever first. Groin pain: ball squeeze isometrics.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 15 to 30s each side
exercises.progress_by: Short → long lever, add leg raises
exercises.regress_by: Ball squeeze, side lying adduction

exercises.name: Supine Hip Internal Rotation
exercises.why: Hip internal and external rotation are often the first ranges lost with age and are critical for the golf swing, squat depth and low back health (joint by joint).
cues: Sit tall in 90/90 or lie in position
Rotate through the hips, keep the chest tall
Move slowly, hold the end range
exercises.joint_notes: Hip pain: reduce range.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Hands free, hip lifts, longer holds
exercises.regress_by: Hands support

exercises.name: Prone Hip Internal Rotation
exercises.why: Hip internal and external rotation are often the first ranges lost with age and are critical for the golf swing, squat depth and low back health (joint by joint).

Rotate through the hips, keep the chest tall

exercises.regress_by: Hands support

exercises.name: Side Plank Hip Abduction
exercises.why: Part of the McGill Big 3. Builds the side core that stabilises the spine when carrying or standing on one leg. Hip abduction versions also train the glute med.
cues: Elbow under the shoulder, body in a straight line
Push the hips up and forward
Breathe and hold
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder pain: kneeling version or suitcase carry instead.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 15 to 45s each side (or 6/4/2 x 10s)
exercises.progress_by: Feet stacked, add hip abduction, Copenhagen
exercises.regress_by: Knees bent side plank

exercises.name: Lying Knee Drops
exercises.why: Gentle spinal mobility for back care and warm ups. Extension drills (prone lying, McKenzie press ups) often ease disc type back pain; flexion drills (knee to chest, child's pose) often ease stiffness and stenosis type pain. Find the direction that helps the individual (McGill: find the pain triggers) and use it.
cues: Move slowly through comfortable range
Breathe out into the end range
Stop if symptoms travel down a leg
exercises.joint_notes: Generally very safe. Osteoporosis: avoid repeated or loaded spinal flexion. Pain spreading into a leg: stop and refer.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Bigger range, add breathing holds
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range

exercises.name: Shin Box
exercises.why: Hip internal and external rotation are often the first ranges lost with age and are critical for the golf swing, squat depth and low back health (joint by joint).
cues: Sit tall in 90/90 or lie in position
Rotate through the hips, keep the chest tall
Move slowly, hold the end range

exercises.progress_by: Hands free, hip lifts, longer holds
exercises.regress_by: Hands support

exercises.name: Cossack Squat (Assisted)
exercises.why: Most training is forwards and backwards; lateral lunges train the side to side plane, building adductor strength and hip mobility that protect against groin strains and help golf, tennis and walking on uneven ground. Cossack squats are a great mobility and strength hybrid (Squat University and DeFranco's Limber 11).
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
cues: Step wide to the side, toes forward or slightly out
Sit back into one hip, keeping the other leg straight
Push back to the start through the bent leg
faults: Knee caving on the bent leg
Rounding the back to get lower
exercises.joint_notes: Groin and hip sensitive members: reduce range. Assisted versions (holding the rig) for seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (each side)
exercises.progress_by: Add load (goblet, DB, landmine), slider, deeper cossack
exercises.regress_by: Shorter range, hand support, lateral lunge rock (mobility)

exercises.name: Standing Cable Hip Flexion
exercises.why: Hip flexor strength (especially lifting the knee above 90 degrees) declines with age and affects walking, stairs and tripping. Ben Patrick includes it in ATG Zero.
variation_notes: Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
cues: Sit or lie tall
Lift the knee up without leaning back
Lower slowly
exercises.joint_notes: Gentle and safe. Hip impingement: keep below pain.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
exercises.progress_by: Band resistance, standing, longer holds
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilt (Supine)
exercises.why: Breathing is the foundation of bracing (Chek: breathing first). Crocodile and 90/90 breathing teach 360 degree breathing, calm the nervous system and help back pain and pelvic floor function.
cues: Lie in position, hands on the lower ribs
Breathe in through the nose expanding 360 degrees (belly, sides, back)
Exhale slowly fully, feeling the ribs drop
exercises.joint_notes: Universally safe. Great on RED readiness days.
exercises.prescription: 5 to 10 slow breaths
exercises.progress_by: Add movement (dead bug with breathing)
exercises.regress_by: Shorter sets

exercises.name: Quad Set (Isometric)
exercises.why: First stage quad work for knee pain, after surgery and for replacements. Terminal knee extensions train the last part of straightening the knee, which is often lost.
variation_notes: Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
cues: Tighten the thigh to straighten the knee
Hold 3 to 5s
Lower slowly
faults: Bent knee in straight leg raise
exercises.joint_notes: Rehab friendly.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 x 10 to 15, 3s holds
exercises.progress_by: Add ankle weight, band
exercises.regress_by: No load

exercises.name: Single Leg Balance
exercises.muscles: Foot, ankle, hip stabilisers, nervous system
exercises.why: Balance falls away quickly with age and inactivity; falls are a leading cause of injury in older adults. Single leg balance is part of the Optimal screen. Train it every session for 60+ (Gambetta: postural alignment and dynamic balance are the foundation).
cues: Stand tall near a support
Grip the floor with the foot, soft knee
Hold or reach while keeping the hips level
exercises.joint_notes: Always near a rail or rig for seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 x 20 to 30s each leg
exercises.progress_by: Eyes closed, cushion, reach, catch a ball
exercises.regress_by: Hand on support, tandem stance

exercises.name: Straight Leg Raise
exercises.why: First stage quad work for knee pain, after surgery and for replacements. Terminal knee extensions train the last part of straightening the knee, which is often lost.
cues: Tighten the thigh to straighten the knee
Hold 3 to 5s
Lower slowly
faults: Bent knee in straight leg raise
exercises.joint_notes: Rehab friendly.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 x 10 to 15, 3s holds
exercises.progress_by: Add ankle weight, band
exercises.regress_by: No load

exercises.name: Single Leg Mini Squat
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, adductors, balance and foot control
exercises.why: Single leg squats are the top of Mike Boyle's single leg ladder: maximum leg strength with minimal spinal load, and they expose left/right imbalances. Box versions control depth so they are accessible far earlier than a full pistol.
cues: Stand on one leg, other leg held forward (pistol) or behind (skater/shrimp)
Sit back and down slowly to the box or depth target, knee over the middle of the foot
Drive up through the whole foot without the knee caving
exercises.joint_notes: Demanding on the knee. Use a box and TRX support first. Not for acute knee pain or early post surgery.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 5 to 8 each leg, slow lowering
exercises.progress_by: Lower the box, remove support, add a light counterweight held forward, then load
exercises.regress_by: Higher box, TRX assisted, step downs, split squat

exercises.progress_by: Add ankle weight, band

exercises.name: Tibialis Raise
exercises.why: Ben Patrick's 'bottom up' foundation: the shin muscle balances the calf, decelerates the foot and protects the knee. Wall tib raises take 1 minute and belong in every lower body warm up.
cues: Back against a wall, heels 30 to 50cm away
Lift the toes up as high as possible
Lower slowly
exercises.joint_notes: Universally safe.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 x 20 to 25
exercises.progress_by: Feet further from the wall, single leg, tib bar load
exercises.regress_by: Closer to the wall

exercises.name: Seated Knee Extension (Ankle Weight)

exercises.name: Calf Raise (Straight Knee)
exercises.muscles: Calves (gastrocnemius straight knee, soleus bent knee), Achilles
exercises.why: Strong calves protect the knee and Achilles and power walking. Ben Patrick's ATG insists on full range (stretch at the bottom). Bent knee versions train the soleus, critical for running and walking endurance.
cues: Full stretch at the bottom
Rise to the highest point on the big toe
Pause, lower slowly (3s)
faults: Rolling to the outside of the foot
exercises.joint_notes: Achilles pain: slow heavy calf raises are rehab gold.
exercises.prescription: 3 x 12 to 20 (slow)
exercises.progress_by: Single leg, off a step, add load
exercises.regress_by: Two legs, hand support, flat floor

exercises.name: Heel Slides
exercises.why: Gentle knee bending range work, used after injury or surgery.
cues: Slide the heel towards the bum slowly
Stop at gentle stretch
Return
exercises.joint_notes: Rehab friendly.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Bigger range
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range

exercises.name: Isometric Wall Sit
exercises.why: A simple, joint friendly way to build quad strength and endurance with zero technique demand. Isometrics can reduce knee pain and are ideal for beginners, seniors and anyone who cannot yet squat through full range. The Swiss ball version lets people practise the squat path with support.
variation_notes: Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
cues: Back flat against the wall, feet hip width and slightly in front
Slide down until the knees are at a pain free angle (aim 90 degrees over time)
Weight through the whole foot, breathe slowly, knees in line with toes
faults: Going too deep too soon and aggravating knees
exercises.joint_notes: Very knee friendly at higher positions. Adjust depth to stay at or below 3/10 pain. Avoid long holds with breath holding for members with high blood pressure.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 45s holds, rest 60s, about 70% effort
exercises.progress_by: Lower the position, hold longer, hold a plate, progress to single leg wall sit or tempo goblet squats
exercises.regress_by: Higher position, shorter holds, hands on thighs for the first few sessions

exercises.name: Hamstring Curl (Swiss Ball)
exercises.why: Hamstrings both extend the hip and bend the knee; curls train the knee bending role that RDLs miss. Strong hamstrings protect knees and reduce hamstring strain risk. Nordic curls are among the best researched injury prevention exercises.
variation_notes: Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
cues: Lie on your back, heels on the ball/sliders/TRX, lift the hips
Curl the heels towards the bum keeping the hips high
Extend slowly back out (control is the exercise)
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly. Nordics are demanding: use band assistance and partial range, expect soreness at first.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
exercises.progress_by: Hips stay up throughout, single leg, slower lowering, Nordic progression
exercises.regress_by: Hips on the floor curl, eccentric only, double leg

exercises.name: Spanish Squat Isometric
exercises.why: A band behind the knees lets the shins stay vertical while the hips sit back, so the quads work hard with very little compressive stress on the front of the knee. Isometric holds like this are one of the best known tools for calming irritable knees (patellar tendon and kneecap pain) while still loading the quads. A Squat University and physio favourite.
variation_notes: Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
cues: Heavy band behind both knees anchored to the rig, walk back until it is tight
Sit back and down until thighs are around 60 to 90 degrees, shins vertical
Keep chest proud, push knees back into the band and hold
faults: Letting the knees drift forward off the band
Holding the breath for the whole set
Going so deep that pain rises above 3/10
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly by design. Often reduces knee pain for several hours afterwards, which makes it a great warm up before squatting for sore knees. Back is upright so low back load is minimal.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 45s holds, rest 60s, about 70% effort (5 x 45s is a classic tendon dose)
exercises.progress_by: Hold longer (45s), sit deeper, add a weight held at the chest, progress to tempo goblet squats and Poliquin step ups
exercises.regress_by: Shorten the hold, sit less deep, lighter band, switch to a wall sit with a higher position

Curl the heels towards the bum keeping the hips high

exercises.progress_by: Hips stay up throughout, single leg, slower lowering, Nordic progression
exercises.regress_by: Hips on the floor curl, eccentric only, double leg

exercises.joint_notes: Rehab friendly.

exercises.progress_by: Add ankle weight, band
exercises.regress_by: No load

exercises.name: Box Squat (High Box)
exercises.why: The box sets a consistent, safe depth and teaches people to sit back and control the descent. It is the best teaching squat for beginners and painful knees and, with a barbell or SSB, a classic DeFranco/Westside strength builder.
variation_notes: Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Box at a height where the spine stays neutral
Sit back and down with control, touch the box lightly (don't crash)
Stay braced, drive up through the whole foot
faults: Plonking down and relaxing on the box
exercises.joint_notes: Excellent for knee pain and older members: adjust height to the pain free range. Lower the box as mobility and control improve.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Lower the box, add load (goblet then SSB/barbell), pause on the box without relaxing, remove the box
exercises.regress_by: Raise the box, TRX assisted box squat, sit to stand

exercises.name: Goblet Squat to Box
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core
exercises.why: Holding the weight at the chest counterbalances the body, so people naturally squat more upright and deeper with better form. Dan John and Squat University both use it as THE teaching squat, and it is strong enough to stay useful for years. Fits groups perfectly because load scales from a 4kg KB to a 40kg+ DB.
variation_notes: Combination move: trains two qualities at once, efficient for HYBRID and BURN; keep technique of both parts clean before speeding up.
cues: Hold the bell tight to the chest, elbows pointing down
Push the knees out and sit between the hips, chest proud
Drive up through the whole foot, squeeze the glutes at the top
faults: Rounding the upper back and letting the weight pull you forward
Knees caving inward on the way up
exercises.joint_notes: Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat
exercises.regress_by: Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell

exercises.name: Bike (Low Resistance)
exercises.muscles: Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
exercises.why: The bike, rower and ski erg give big conditioning with no impact, and every level can work at their own intensity. Zone 2 builds the aerobic base (Attia); short sprints suit menopause and fat loss (Sims, Cosgrove hierarchy). Backward walking (treadmill or sled) is Ben Patrick's knee warm up.
cues: Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence
Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs
Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips
faults: Going out too hard in intervals
exercises.joint_notes: Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
exercises.prescription: Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
exercises.progress_by: Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds
exercises.regress_by: Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest

exercises.name: Reverse Sled Drag
exercises.why: Ben Patrick's number one knee tool: walking backwards loads the quads with the knee travelling over the toes, floods the knee with blood and is nearly impossible to overdo.
cues: Lean back slightly against the sled (or hold the treadmill rails)
Small steps, push through the front of the foot
Knees travel over the toes
exercises.joint_notes: Knee pain staple. Very safe.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 min warm up, or 4 to 6 x 20m
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, longer
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, treadmill flat

exercises.name: Patellar Mobilisation
exercises.why: Foam rolling reduces the sensation of stiffness and prepares tissues for movement (Cosgrove template step 1). Short, targeted, before the session.
cues: Roll slowly
Pause on tender spots and breathe
30 to 60s per area
exercises.joint_notes: Avoid rolling directly on bones, varicose veins or acute injuries.
exercises.prescription: 30 to 60s per area
exercises.progress_by: Firmer tools
exercises.regress_by: Softer roller

30 to 60s per area
exercises.joint_notes: Avoid rolling directly on bones, varicose veins or acute injuries.
exercises.prescription: 30 to 60s per area
exercises.progress_by: Firmer tools
exercises.regress_by: Softer roller

exercises.name: Forward Step Down
exercises.why: Controlled lowering from a step builds knee control and eccentric quad strength, the exact quality needed for walking downstairs. Also a key screening test for knee valgus and hip control.
cues: Stand on a box, other leg hanging off the front or side
Lower slowly by bending the standing knee, hips back slightly
Tap the heel lightly and return without pushing off the floor
faults: Hip dropping on the free side
exercises.joint_notes: Excellent for knee rehab when the box is low. Raise the height as control improves.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 8 to 12 each leg, 3s lowering
exercises.progress_by: Higher box, hold weight, slower lowering
exercises.regress_by: Lower box, hand support, Poliquin step up

exercises.name: Quad Stretch (Standing)
exercises.muscles: Target muscles and joints vary (named in the exercise)
exercises.why: Static and gentle mobility work restores range lost from sitting and ageing. Best used where a screen shows a restriction (Squat University: screen, correct, retest), and to cool down. McKenzie press ups and extension work often relieve disc type back pain; flexion stretches often suit stenosis type pain: individualise.
cues: Get into position slowly
Breathe out to relax into range, no bouncing
Hold 30 to 60s or do slow reps
faults: Stretching instead of strengthening when stability is the issue
exercises.joint_notes: Gentle and safe. Stop if symptoms travel down the leg. Osteoporosis: avoid loaded flexion stretches.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Longer holds, deeper range, add loaded stretching
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range, supported versions

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch (Supine)
exercises.muscles: Target muscles and joints vary (named in the exercise)

exercises.name: Knee to Wall Ankle Mobility
exercises.why: Stiff ankles cause heels lifting, knees caving and forward lean in squats, and pain further up the chain (joint by joint). The knee to wall test is the screen; rocks and banded mobs are the fix (Squat University).
cues: Half kneeling, foot about 10cm from the wall
Drive the knee forward over the toes keeping the heel down
Rock in and out
exercises.joint_notes: Universally safe.
exercises.prescription: 2 x 10 to 15 rocks each side
exercises.progress_by: Further from the wall, band, load
exercises.regress_by: Closer to the wall

exercises.name: Split Squat (Short Range)
exercises.why: The entry point of the single leg ladder. A static split stance gives a stable base, so people learn to load one leg at a time safely. It builds balance, fixes imbalances and is far easier on the back than heavy bilateral squats. Front foot elevated adds knee travel (ATG style); cable and landmine versions add stability.
variation_notes: Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Long split stance, both feet pointing forward, hip width apart
Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor
Push through the front foot to stand, keep the torso tall
faults: Lunging forward instead of dropping down
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly when depth is controlled. Use a pad under the back knee. Hold a support for balance in seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Add load, elevate the front foot (ATG style), then elevate the back foot (RFESS)
exercises.regress_by: TRX or rig assisted split squat, shorter range, isometric split squat hold
