exercises.name: Sissy Squat (Assisted, Short Range)
exercises.muscles: Quads (rectus femoris in a lengthened position), hip flexors
exercises.why: Trains the quads with the knees travelling far over the toes and the hips extended. Builds strength in the end range of knee bending, which Ben Patrick uses to bulletproof knees. Assisted versions are surprisingly accessible.
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Hold a post or TRX for support
Rise onto the toes, push the knees forward and lean the body back as one straight line from knee to shoulder
Lower only as far as pain free, drive back up through the quads
faults: Bending at the hips (turns it into a normal squat)
Letting go of the support before ready
exercises.joint_notes: Earn it. Start short range with hand support. Avoid with acute knee pain, recent knee surgery or knee replacements unless cleared.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 12 reps, slow lowering, hand support
exercises.progress_by: Increase range, reduce hand assistance, add a plate at the chest, progress towards reverse Nordic
exercises.regress_by: Short range only, more hand support, swap to Spanish squat or heels elevated goblet squat

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge (Slider)
exercises.why: Stepping backwards keeps the shin more vertical, so it is far kinder to the knees than forward lunges while still training single leg strength and balance. The default lunge at Optimal. Deficit and slider versions increase range and control.
variation_notes: Sliders add a friction based eccentric control challenge.
cues: Stand tall, step one foot back
Drop the back knee towards the floor, front shin fairly vertical
Drive through the front heel to stand back up
exercises.joint_notes: Most knee friendly lunge. Use a pad and hand support for beginners.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Add load, deficit (front foot on a plate), knee drive at the top, barbell/landmine
exercises.regress_by: Split squat (static), hand support, shorter range

exercises.name: Pogo Hops (Low)
exercises.muscles: Whole lower body, tendons, nervous system
exercises.why: Jumps and hops train power, tendon stiffness and bone (impact is a key bone stimulus in LIFTMOR). Landings (snap downs, drop squats, jump and stick) teach the body to absorb force, the foundation of injury prevention. Progress carefully: landing before jumping, low before high, two legs before one.
cues: Land softly and quietly, hips back, knees over toes
Stick the landing for a second before the next rep
Quality over quantity: stop when height or control drops
faults: Landing stiff legged or with knees caving
Too many reps (plyos are not cardio)
exercises.joint_notes: IMPACT: excluded from Optimal GROUP sessions (no jumping rule). Teams only after screening. Avoid with pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis with fracture history, joint replacements, acute knee/Achilles pain.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 sets x 3 to 6 reps, full recovery (60 to 120s), stop when speed drops; 2 to 3 sessions/week max, low total contacts (20 to 60)
exercises.progress_by: Landings → small jumps → box jumps → broad jumps → single leg hops → depth jumps
exercises.regress_by: Snap downs/drop squat and stick, step ups, sled push, med ball throws
exercises.group_alternative: Group swap (no jumping): sled push, fast step ups, med ball chest pass or slam, KB swing, fast sit to stand

exercises.name: Single Leg Sit to Stand
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, adductors, balance and foot control
exercises.why: Single leg squats are the top of Mike Boyle's single leg ladder: maximum leg strength with minimal spinal load, and they expose left/right imbalances. Box versions control depth so they are accessible far earlier than a full pistol.
cues: Stand on one leg, other leg held forward (pistol) or behind (skater/shrimp)
Sit back and down slowly to the box or depth target, knee over the middle of the foot
Drive up through the whole foot without the knee caving
exercises.joint_notes: Demanding on the knee. Use a box and TRX support first. Not for acute knee pain or early post surgery.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 5 to 8 each leg, slow lowering
exercises.progress_by: Lower the box, remove support, add a light counterweight held forward, then load
exercises.regress_by: Higher box, TRX assisted, step downs, split squat

exercises.name: Sit to Stand (Chair)
exercises.why: The most important real life squat: getting up from a chair or toilet. A key longevity skill and a core test for seniors (30 second sit to stand). Done fast on the way up, it trains power, which declines faster than strength with age.
cues: Sit tall on a box or chair, feet slightly back under the knees
Lean the chest forward, push the floor away and stand up tall
Sit back down slowly with control, don't flop
faults: Using the hands to push off
Collapsing back down onto the seat
exercises.joint_notes: Suitable for almost everyone. Raise the seat height for painful knees or hips. Single leg version needs good knee control.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps (or max reps in 30s for testing), stand up fast, lower slowly
exercises.progress_by: Lower the box, hold a weight at the chest, stand up as fast as possible (power), single leg sit to stand
exercises.regress_by: Raise the seat, use hands on thighs or a TRX for help, reduce reps

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing (Crocodile)
exercises.why: Breathing is the foundation of bracing (Chek: breathing first). Crocodile and 90/90 breathing teach 360 degree breathing, calm the nervous system and help back pain and pelvic floor function.
cues: Lie in position, hands on the lower ribs
Breathe in through the nose expanding 360 degrees (belly, sides, back)
Exhale slowly fully, feeling the ribs drop
exercises.joint_notes: Universally safe. Great on RED readiness days.
exercises.prescription: 5 to 10 slow breaths
exercises.progress_by: Add movement (dead bug with breathing)
exercises.regress_by: Shorter sets

exercises.name: Stir the Pot
exercises.pattern: Core: anti extension + anti rotation (Swiss ball)
exercises.why: McGill's favourite advanced core drill: forearms on a Swiss ball making small circles while the body stays rigid.
cues: Forearms on the ball, plank position
Draw small circles with the elbows
Keep the hips and back still
exercises.joint_notes: Safe for backs when form is held. Shoulder pain: reduce range.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 x 5 to 10 circles each way
exercises.progress_by: Bigger circles, feet narrower
exercises.regress_by: Swiss ball plank hold

exercises.name: Swiss Ball Rollout (Short Range)
exercises.why: Rollouts and body saws are advanced anti extension: the further the arms reach, the harder the core works to stop the back arching.
variation_notes: Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Kneeling or plank, ribs down, glutes tight
Roll or slide out only as far as you can keep the back flat
Pull back using the abs and lats
exercises.joint_notes: Can strain the low back if overreached. Shoulder pain: limit range.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
exercises.progress_by: Longer range, from feet
exercises.regress_by: Swiss ball rollout short range, plank

exercises.name: Reverse Hyper (Bench, Light)
exercises.why: Strengthens the back extensors and glutes, improving posture and back resilience. Reverse hypers decompress the spine as they train. Extend to neutral only: the goal is a strong, straight spine, not arching.
variation_notes: Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Hinge at the hips, keep the spine long
Lift to a straight line from head to heels using the glutes
Lower with control
faults: Rounding heavily at the bottom under load
exercises.joint_notes: Good for most back pain when kept to neutral. Avoid loaded flexion at the bottom for osteoporosis.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
exercises.progress_by: Hold a plate, single leg, pause at the top
exercises.regress_by: Superman, bird dog, shorter range

exercises.name: Cat Cow
exercises.why: Gentle spinal mobility for back care and warm ups. Extension drills (prone lying, McKenzie press ups) often ease disc type back pain; flexion drills (knee to chest, child's pose) often ease stiffness and stenosis type pain. Find the direction that helps the individual (McGill: find the pain triggers) and use it.
cues: Move slowly through comfortable range
Breathe out into the end range
Stop if symptoms travel down a leg
exercises.joint_notes: Generally very safe. Osteoporosis: avoid repeated or loaded spinal flexion. Pain spreading into a leg: stop and refer.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Bigger range, add breathing holds
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range

Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg while breathing out

exercises.name: Front Plank (Short Hold)
exercises.why: The plank trains the core to resist extension. Useful foundation, part of the Optimal screen (30s kneeling → full plank → plank with full tension). Long lever and RKC versions dramatically increase difficulty without longer holds.
variation_notes: Isometric: builds strength and tendon tolerance in a fixed position with minimal joint irritation.
cues: Elbows under shoulders, straight line head to heels
Squeeze glutes, pull the ribs down, push the floor away
Breathe, hold with full tension
faults: Holding for minutes with poor form
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder or wrist pain: dead bug or Pallof press instead. Prefer 20 to 30s high tension holds over long sloppy ones.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 20 to 40s (high tension)
exercises.progress_by: Long lever, RKC plank, leg lift, body saw
exercises.regress_by: Plank on knees, incline plank on a bench

exercises.name: QL Stretch (Side Lean)
exercises.muscles: Target muscles and joints vary (named in the exercise)
exercises.why: Static and gentle mobility work restores range lost from sitting and ageing. Best used where a screen shows a restriction (Squat University: screen, correct, retest), and to cool down. McKenzie press ups and extension work often relieve disc type back pain; flexion stretches often suit stenosis type pain: individualise.
cues: Get into position slowly
Breathe out to relax into range, no bouncing
Hold 30 to 60s or do slow reps
faults: Stretching instead of strengthening when stability is the issue
exercises.joint_notes: Gentle and safe. Stop if symptoms travel down the leg. Osteoporosis: avoid loaded flexion stretches.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Longer holds, deeper range, add loaded stretching
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range, supported versions

exercises.muscles: Target muscles and joints vary (named in the exercise)

exercises.name: Walking (Treadmill)
exercises.muscles: Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
exercises.why: The bike, rower and ski erg give big conditioning with no impact, and every level can work at their own intensity. Zone 2 builds the aerobic base (Attia); short sprints suit menopause and fat loss (Sims, Cosgrove hierarchy). Backward walking (treadmill or sled) is Ben Patrick's knee warm up.
cues: Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence
Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs
Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips
faults: Going out too hard in intervals
exercises.joint_notes: Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
exercises.prescription: Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
exercises.progress_by: Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds
exercises.regress_by: Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest

exercises.name: Glute Bridge March
exercises.why: Bridges and hip thrusts train the glutes at their strongest point (full hip extension) with almost no spinal load. They are essential for back pain, knee pain, posture, sprinting and golf power, and are safe for nearly everyone. Single leg versions fix imbalances.
cues: Feet flat, shins vertical at the top
Tuck the ribs down, drive through the heels and squeeze the glutes to lift
Pause at the top without arching the low back, lower slowly
faults: Arching the low back instead of extending the hips
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly. Use a pad on the hips when loaded. Shoulder elevated versions need a stable bench.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9 (pause 1 to 2s at the top)
exercises.progress_by: Bridge → hip thrust off a bench → load (DB, barbell) → single leg, add pauses or bands
exercises.regress_by: Floor bridge, shorter range, isometric hold

exercises.name: Hip Hinge to Wall
exercises.why: Teaches people to move at the hips not the spine. The dowel gives instant feedback (head, upper back and tailbone stay in contact). Every hinge exercise depends on this skill, so McGill and Squat University teach it first.
cues: Dowel along the spine touching head, upper back and tailbone
Soft knees, push the hips back as if closing a car door with your bum
Hinge until you feel the hamstrings, keep all three contact points, stand back up
faults: Losing the dowel contact at the low back
Bending the knees into a squat
Looking up and cranking the neck
exercises.joint_notes: Ideal for back pain members. No load, no risk.
exercises.prescription: 2 sets x 8 to 10 slow reps (warm up)
exercises.progress_by: Hold a KB at the chest, progress to KB deadlift from blocks
exercises.regress_by: Hinge to a wall (bum touches the wall) with a smaller range

exercises.name: Cable Pull Through (Light)
exercises.why: Cable/band pull throughs teach the hip hinge with the load pulling from behind, so people naturally sit the hips back and finish with the glutes. Kickbacks and quadruped hip extensions isolate the glutes for activation and rehab.
variation_notes: Cable: constant tension through the whole range with smooth, joint friendly resistance.
Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Face away from the cable, rope between the legs
Hinge back letting the rope pull the hips back
Drive the hips through and squeeze the glutes, stand tall
exercises.joint_notes: Very back friendly. A great swing and deadlift regression.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, pause at the top, progress to KB swing
exercises.regress_by: Band version, shorter range

exercises.name: KB Deadlift (Elevated)
exercises.why: The safest way to teach lifting from the floor. Picking things up is a life skill (Primal Pattern 'bend'). Raising the bell on blocks reduces range for beginners and back pain; suitcase versions add anti lateral flexion.
cues: Bell between the feet (or beside for suitcase), hinge down with a flat back
Grip, pull the shoulders down, brace
Push the floor away and stand tall, squeeze the glutes
exercises.joint_notes: Very back friendly. Elevate the bell on a step for limited hip mobility or back history.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, double KB, lower to the floor, progress to RDL, swing and trap bar
exercises.regress_by: Bell on a block/step, hinge drill

exercises.name: Suitcase Deadlift (Light)
exercises.why: The safest way to teach lifting from the floor. Picking things up is a life skill (Primal Pattern 'bend'). Raising the bell on blocks reduces range for beginners and back pain; suitcase versions add anti lateral flexion.
variation_notes: One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
Reduced range/load version: used for rehab, beginners, warm ups or flare up days.
cues: Bell between the feet (or beside for suitcase), hinge down with a flat back
Grip, pull the shoulders down, brace
Push the floor away and stand tall, squeeze the glutes
exercises.joint_notes: Very back friendly. Elevate the bell on a step for limited hip mobility or back history.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, double KB, lower to the floor, progress to RDL, swing and trap bar
exercises.regress_by: Bell on a block/step, hinge drill

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.why: One side loading turns a carry into an anti lateral flexion core exercise: you must stop the body leaning. McGill calls the suitcase carry one of the best core exercises.
variation_notes: One sided loading adds an anti rotation / anti lateral flexion core challenge and exposes left/right differences.
cues: Weight in one hand, stand tall, shoulders level
Walk slowly without leaning towards or away from the weight
Swap hands
exercises.joint_notes: Back pain friendly.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s each side
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, march with high knees, longer
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, static hold

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.why: Dan John says loaded carries change lives. Picking up heavy things and walking trains grip (a strong longevity predictor), posture, core and conditioning all at once, with low technical demand and low injury risk. Every member, every week.
cues: Deadlift the weights up properly
Stand tall, shoulders down, walk with short controlled steps
Breathe and keep the ribs down
faults: Leaning forward or side to side
exercises.joint_notes: Very safe. Pick up and put down with a good hinge. Grip limited members: straps are fine to train the rest.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 x 20 to 40m (or 30 to 45s), rest 60 to 90s
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, longer, on the toes, with steps/obstacles; Dan John standard: bodyweight total for men
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, shorter, static hold

exercises.name: Side Lying Clam
exercises.muscles: Glute medius and minimus, hip stabilisers
exercises.why: The side glutes stop the knee caving and the pelvis dropping when on one leg. Weak glute meds are linked to knee pain, hip pain and back pain. Simple band work fixes it and works brilliantly as a warm up (Squat University, Boyle).
cues: Athletic stance, band around the knees or ankles
Push the knees out, step sideways (or lift the leg) leading with the heel
Stay low and keep the pelvis level
faults: Rocking the torso side to side
Letting the band pull the knees in
exercises.joint_notes: Very joint friendly, ideal for hip and knee rehab.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each side
exercises.progress_by: Heavier band, band lower on the leg, side plank abduction
exercises.regress_by: Side lying with no band, smaller range

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.why: The core's main job is to stop unwanted movement. The Pallof press resists the cable pulling you round, training the anti rotation strength that protects the back and transfers force in golf, tennis and lifting (McGill, Boyle, Cosgrove).
cues: Side on to the cable at chest height, brace
Press the handle straight out from the chest and hold 2s
Don't let the hands or hips rotate, return to the chest
exercises.joint_notes: Excellent for back pain. Half kneeling reduces hip involvement and isolates the core.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
exercises.progress_by: Tall kneeling → half kneeling → split → standing → walkouts, add overhead reach, heavier
exercises.regress_by: Lighter band, closer to the anchor, iso hold

exercises.name: Supine Hollow Hold (Tuck)
exercises.why: A gymnastic anti extension hold. Harder than a dead bug.
cues: Low back pressed down
Arms and legs extended low
Hold
exercises.joint_notes: Can strain the low back if form is lost. Tuck the knees to regress.
exercises.prescription: 3 x 15 to 30s
exercises.progress_by: Longer levers, rocks
exercises.regress_by: Tuck hold, dead bug

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.why: Dynamic drills raise temperature, take joints through range and rehearse patterns (RAMP warm up). The World's Greatest Stretch hits hip flexors, hamstrings, adductors and T spine in one move. 40+ members need a full 8 to 10 minute warm up every session.
cues: Move through big comfortable ranges
Increase range each rep
Breathe and stay controlled
exercises.joint_notes: Safe for almost everyone.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 x 5 to 10 each side (or 20 to 30m)
exercises.progress_by: Bigger range, add reaches
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range, hand support

exercises.name: Dowel Overhead Squat
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, upper back, shoulders, core
exercises.why: The overhead squat exposes stiffness at the ankles, hips, T spine and shoulders all at once, which is why Squat University and the FMS use it as a screen. With a dowel it is an excellent mobility drill; loaded it is a high skill G4 lift.
cues: Arms locked overhead, biceps by the ears, push up into the dowel or weight
Sit down between the hips with the chest proud
Keep the bar over the middle of the foot throughout
faults: Lower back rounding at the bottom
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder demanding: avoid loading with shoulder pain or impingement. Use a dowel as a warm up screen instead.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 5 to 8 reps, light, slow
exercises.progress_by: Dowel → light DB/plate → barbell overhead squat
exercises.regress_by: Dowel only, squat to a box, heels elevated, arms in a Y position

exercises.name: Downward Dog to Cobra
exercises.why: Gentle spinal mobility for back care and warm ups. Extension drills (prone lying, McKenzie press ups) often ease disc type back pain; flexion drills (knee to chest, child's pose) often ease stiffness and stenosis type pain. Find the direction that helps the individual (McGill: find the pain triggers) and use it.

Breathe out into the end range
Stop if symptoms travel down a leg

exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Bigger range, add breathing holds
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range

exercises.name: Open Book
exercises.muscles: Thoracic spine rotation and extension, lats, pecs
exercises.why: The upper back should move; the low back should be stable (joint by joint). Stiff upper backs cause rounded posture, shoulder pain and low back pain, and limit the golf swing. Daily T spine drills fix it.
cues: Keep the hips still (knee pinned or in quadruped)
Rotate/extend through the upper back, follow the hand with the eyes
Breathe out into the end range
exercises.joint_notes: Very safe. Osteoporosis: avoid forced flexion; gentle rotation and extension are fine.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 sets x 5 to 10 slow reps (or 30 to 60s), in warm up or cool down
exercises.progress_by: Add a reach, hold end range longer
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range, seated version

exercises.name: Patrick Step
exercises.pattern: Single leg: knee over toes step (VMO)
exercises.why: Ben Patrick's entry level knee builder from ATG Zero: standing on a low step on the ball of the foot, the knee travels forward over the toes as the other heel lowers to tap the floor. It teaches the quads, not the joint, to own the knees over toes position and is the first step towards the ATG split squat.
cues: Stand on a low step, working heel raised on a small plate or wedge (Poliquin) or on the toes (Patrick)
Slowly lower the other heel towards the floor by bending the working knee forward over the toes
Lightly tap and drive back up through the front of the foot, keeping the knee in line
faults: Hips shifting back instead of the knee travelling forward
Dropping fast instead of controlling the lowering
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly when kept pain free. Start with a very low step (5 to 10cm) and hand support. Ideal in every knee pain programme.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 20 each leg, slow lowering (3s)
exercises.progress_by: Higher step, slower tempo, hold DBs, progress to step downs and front foot elevated split squats
exercises.regress_by: Lower step, hand on the rig, partial range

exercises.name: ATG Split Squat
exercises.why: Ben Patrick's signature exercise: a long split squat where the front knee travels well past the toes with the heel staying down and the back knee lowers to the floor, giving a deep hip flexor stretch on the back leg. It builds strength in the deepest knee position and hip flexor flexibility at the same time. Start with the front foot elevated and hand support, hold the bottom for time (e.g. 30s), then add reps and load.
cues: Long split stance, both feet pointing forward, hip width apart
Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor
Push through the front foot to stand, keep the torso tall
faults: Lunging forward instead of dropping down
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly when depth is controlled. Use a pad under the back knee. Hold a support for balance in seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 (each leg)
exercises.progress_by: Add load, elevate the front foot (ATG style), then elevate the back foot (RFESS)
exercises.regress_by: TRX or rig assisted split squat, shorter range, isometric split squat hold

exercises.name: Front Foot Elevated ATG Split Squat (Assisted)
exercises.why: The regression Ben Patrick uses before the floor level ATG split squat: front foot on a step and hands on a support so the knee can travel over the toes in a pain free range.
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).

Lower the back knee straight down towards the floor
Push through the front foot to stand, keep the torso tall

exercises.name: Reverse Nordic (Assisted)
exercises.muscles: Quads (rectus femoris in a lengthened position), hip flexors
exercises.why: Kneeling, the body leans back as one line from knee to head, lengthening and strengthening the quads (especially rectus femoris) through a range most people never train. Ben Patrick uses it for knee resilience and hip flexor length. Use a band or partner for assistance and short range first.
variation_notes: Assisted version: support lets members practise the full pattern safely while strength builds (Cosgrove: regress to progress).
cues: Hold a post or TRX for support
Rise onto the toes, push the knees forward and lean the body back as one straight line from knee to shoulder
Lower only as far as pain free, drive back up through the quads
faults: Bending at the hips (turns it into a normal squat)
Letting go of the support before ready
exercises.joint_notes: Earn it. Start short range with hand support. Avoid with acute knee pain, recent knee surgery or knee replacements unless cleared.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 12 reps, slow lowering, hand support
exercises.progress_by: Increase range, reduce hand assistance, add a plate at the chest, progress towards reverse Nordic
exercises.regress_by: Short range only, more hand support, swap to Spanish squat or heels elevated goblet squat

exercises.name: KOT Calf Raise

cues: Full stretch at the bottom
Rise to the highest point on the big toe
Pause, lower slowly (3s)
faults: Rolling to the outside of the foot
exercises.joint_notes: Achilles pain: slow heavy calf raises are rehab gold.
exercises.prescription: 3 x 12 to 20 (slow)
exercises.progress_by: Single leg, off a step, add load
exercises.regress_by: Two legs, hand support, flat floor

exercises.name: Tib Bar Tibialis Raise
exercises.why: Loaded tibialis raise using a tib bar or a plate/KB over the feet while seated. Ben Patrick's advanced standard is around 25% bodyweight for 5 x 5. Strong shins protect the knees and ankles and balance the calves.
cues: Back against a wall, heels 30 to 50cm away
Lift the toes up as high as possible
Lower slowly
exercises.joint_notes: Universally safe.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 x 20 to 25
exercises.progress_by: Feet further from the wall, single leg, tib bar load
exercises.regress_by: Closer to the wall

exercises.name: Slant Board Goblet Squat
exercises.muscles: Quads, glutes, adductors, upper back, core
exercises.why: Squatting with the heels on a slant board lets the knees travel well forward with the torso upright, loading the quads and VMO with less ankle demand. A Ben Patrick and Squat University tool for knee health and quad strength.

Push the knees out and sit between the hips, chest proud
Drive up through the whole foot, squeeze the glutes at the top
faults: Rounding the upper back and letting the weight pull you forward
Knees caving inward on the way up
exercises.joint_notes: Knee and back friendly. Heels elevated version helps stiff ankles. Use a box for depth control with knee pain. Upper back can fatigue first as loads get heavy.

exercises.progress_by: Add load, tempo (4-1-1-0), pause at the bottom, 1.5 reps, move to double KB front squat or SSB squat
exercises.regress_by: Goblet squat to a box, TRX assisted squat, lighter bell

exercises.name: SSB Squat
exercises.why: The safety squat bar lets members back squat heavy without needing shoulder mobility to hold a straight bar, and its forward pitch keeps the torso upright. It is Optimal's main heavy squat tool for 40+ members with cranky shoulders, elbows or wrists. DeFranco built his reputation using it.

cues: Handles in front, pads on the upper back, brace 360 degrees before descending
Push knees out over the middle of the foot, sit between the hips
Drive up with the chest leading, don't let the bar tip you forward
faults: Letting the bar pull the chest forward and rounding the upper back
Losing the brace at the bottom
Cutting depth as the weight goes up

exercises.why: Professor Stuart McGill's daily core routine for back health: modified curl up, side plank and bird dog, each held 8 to 10 seconds in a descending pyramid (e.g. 6, 4, 2 reps). Builds core endurance and stiffness without stressing the discs. Default warm up for any member with back history.
cues: Lie on your back, one knee bent, hands under the low back
Brace and lift the head and shoulders slightly as one unit
Hold 8 to 10s, lower
exercises.joint_notes: Back pain friendly. Part of the Big 3.

exercises.progress_by: Raise elbows off the floor, longer holds

exercises.name: 4 Point TVA Draw In (Chek)
exercises.why: Paul Chek's inner unit drill: on hands and knees, let the belly relax then draw the belly button gently towards the spine without moving the spine, hold and breathe. Teaches deep core activation before loading (stabilisers before prime movers).
cues: Lie in position, hands on the lower ribs
Breathe in through the nose expanding 360 degrees (belly, sides, back)
Exhale slowly fully, feeling the ribs drop
exercises.joint_notes: Universally safe. Great on RED readiness days.
exercises.prescription: 5 to 10 slow breaths
exercises.progress_by: Add movement (dead bug with breathing)
exercises.regress_by: Shorter sets

exercises.name: Prone Cobra (Chek)
exercises.why: Paul Chek's postural endurance exercise: lying face down, lift the chest slightly and rotate the thumbs out to squeeze the shoulder blades, hold. Strengthens the upper back and spinal extensors that hold upright posture.
cues: Hinge at the hips, keep the spine long
Lift to a straight line from head to heels using the glutes
Lower with control
faults: Rounding heavily at the bottom under load
exercises.joint_notes: Good for most back pain when kept to neutral. Avoid loaded flexion at the bottom for osteoporosis.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 10 to 15 reps, tempo 2-1-1-1, rest 45 to 60s, RPE 8
exercises.progress_by: Hold a plate, single leg, pause at the top
exercises.regress_by: Superman, bird dog, shorter range

exercises.name: Swiss Ball Supine Lateral Ball Roll (Chek)
exercises.why: Paul Chek's twist pattern exercise: lying with the shoulders on a Swiss ball and hips up, arms out holding a light weight, shuffle sideways across the ball keeping the body level. Trains rotational stability of the trunk and hips.
variation_notes: Swiss ball adds instability for core control (Paul Chek); keep loads modest.
cues: Arms long, pivot the back foot
Turn from the hips and upper back together
Control the return through the middle
faults: Rotating only at the low back
exercises.joint_notes: Avoid fast loaded rotation with acute back pain.
exercises.prescription: 2 to 3 sets x 6 to 10 reps each side (or 20 to 40s), slow and controlled
exercises.progress_by: Heavier, faster, split stance
exercises.regress_by: Lighter, smaller range, anti rotation instead

exercises.name: Floor to Stand Transfer
exercises.pattern: Total body: Turkish get up / windmill
exercises.muscles: Shoulder stability, core, hips, whole body
exercises.why: Getting down to the floor and back up with as little support as possible. A key longevity skill (Attia, Dan John) and part of the Optimal screen. Progress from using a chair to hands only to no hands.
cues: Eyes on the bell, arm locked
Move through each step slowly: roll to elbow, hand, high bridge, sweep the leg, kneel, stand
Reverse every step with control
exercises.joint_notes: Learn with a shoe or no weight first. Shoulder pain: half get up with no load only.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 reps each side, slow
exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, full get up
exercises.regress_by: Half get up, shoe on the fist, no weight

exercises.name: Half Kneeling to Stand
exercises.pattern: Total body: Turkish get up / windmill
exercises.muscles: Shoulder stability, core, hips, whole body
exercises.why: From half kneeling, stand up without using the hands (then lower back down). Builds the strength and balance needed to get off the floor, and is a stepping stone to the Turkish get up.
variation_notes: Kneeling position locks the hips so the core has to control the trunk and stops the legs cheating.
cues: Eyes on the bell, arm locked
Move through each step slowly: roll to elbow, hand, high bridge, sweep the leg, kneel, stand
Reverse every step with control
exercises.joint_notes: Learn with a shoe or no weight first. Shoulder pain: half get up with no load only.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 5 reps each side, slow
exercises.progress_by: Heavier bell, full get up
exercises.regress_by: Half get up, shoe on the fist, no weight

exercises.name: Fast Sit to Stand (Power)
exercises.why: Stand up from a chair as fast as possible, sit down slowly. Trains power, which declines faster than strength with age, using the safest possible movement. Seniors programme staple.
variation_notes: Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
cues: Sit tall on a box or chair, feet slightly back under the knees
Lean the chest forward, push the floor away and stand up tall
Sit back down slowly with control, don't flop
faults: Using the hands to push off
Collapsing back down onto the seat
exercises.joint_notes: Suitable for almost everyone. Raise the seat height for painful knees or hips. Single leg version needs good knee control.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps (or max reps in 30s for testing), stand up fast, lower slowly
exercises.progress_by: Lower the box, hold a weight at the chest, stand up as fast as possible (power), single leg sit to stand
exercises.regress_by: Raise the seat, use hands on thighs or a TRX for help, reduce reps

exercises.name: Tandem Stance Balance
exercises.muscles: Foot, ankle, hip stabilisers, nervous system
exercises.why: Standing heel to toe (one foot directly in front of the other) near a support. A falls prevention staple and seniors programme warm up.
cues: Stand tall near a support
Grip the floor with the foot, soft knee
Hold or reach while keeping the hips level
exercises.joint_notes: Always near a rail or rig for seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 x 20 to 30s each leg
exercises.progress_by: Eyes closed, cushion, reach, catch a ball
exercises.regress_by: Hand on support, tandem stance

exercises.name: Heel to Toe Walk
exercises.muscles: Foot, ankle, hip stabilisers, nervous system
exercises.why: Walking in a straight line placing the heel directly in front of the toes. Trains dynamic balance and gait (Gambetta: postural alignment and dynamic balance are the foundation).
cues: Stand tall near a support
Grip the floor with the foot, soft knee
Hold or reach while keeping the hips level
exercises.joint_notes: Always near a rail or rig for seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 x 20 to 30s each leg
exercises.progress_by: Eyes closed, cushion, reach, catch a ball
exercises.regress_by: Hand on support, tandem stance

exercises.name: Clock Reach (Single Leg Balance)
exercises.muscles: Foot, ankle, hip stabilisers, nervous system
exercises.why: Standing on one leg and reaching the other foot to points on an imaginary clock. Builds balance, ankle and hip control.
cues: Stand tall near a support
Grip the floor with the foot, soft knee
Hold or reach while keeping the hips level
exercises.joint_notes: Always near a rail or rig for seniors.
exercises.prescription: 3 x 20 to 30s each leg
exercises.progress_by: Eyes closed, cushion, reach, catch a ball
exercises.regress_by: Hand on support, tandem stance

exercises.name: Jumping Chin Up with Drop Landing (LIFTMOR)
exercises.pattern: Vertical pull: pull up / chin up / hangs
exercises.muscles: Lats, upper back, biceps, grip, core
exercises.why: Used in the LIFTMOR trial for postmenopausal bone health: jump to the top of a chin up, lower slowly, then drop and land firmly on both feet. The landing impact loads the hips and spine. Supervised Teams only, screened, no pelvic floor symptoms.
cues: Grip slightly wider than shoulders (chin up: palms facing you)
Pull the shoulder blades down first, then drive the elbows to the ribs
Chin over the bar, lower slowly to straight arms
exercises.joint_notes: Shoulder pain: neutral grip, band assistance. Hanging can irritate some shoulders: build up gradually.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 or total reps
exercises.progress_by: Band assisted → negatives → bodyweight → weighted
exercises.regress_by: Lat pulldown, TRX assisted pull up, scapula pull up, dead hang
exercises.group_alternative: Use a no impact exercise from the same pattern

exercises.name: Heel Drops (Bone Loading)
exercises.muscles: Calves (gastrocnemius straight knee, soleus bent knee), Achilles
exercises.why: Rise onto the toes and drop firmly onto the heels. A low level impact progression used to load bone in members not yet ready for jumps. No flight phase, so it can be used in groups if comfortable.
cues: Full stretch at the bottom
Rise to the highest point on the big toe
Pause, lower slowly (3s)
faults: Rolling to the outside of the foot
exercises.joint_notes: Achilles pain: slow heavy calf raises are rehab gold.
exercises.prescription: 3 x 12 to 20 (slow)
exercises.progress_by: Single leg, off a step, add load
exercises.regress_by: Two legs, hand support, flat floor

exercises.name: Step Back Burpee (No Jump)
exercises.why: The Optimal group burpee: hands down, step back to plank, step in, stand tall. All of the metabolic benefit with no jumping or landing.
cues: Hands down, step or jump back to plank
Chest down (if required), back to feet
Stand tall (jump only if allowed)
exercises.joint_notes: IMPACT when jumping: group sessions use the no jump version (step back, step in, stand). Devil's press and man makers: DB hinge skill required.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 6 x 20 to 40s
exercises.progress_by: Add a press, push up or jump
exercises.regress_by: Step back burpee, incline burpee onto a bench

exercises.name: Squat Thrust to Bench (No Jump)
exercises.why: Hands on a bench, step back and in. A no impact, wrist friendly burpee regression for groups and seniors.
cues: Hands down, step or jump back to plank
Chest down (if required), back to feet
Stand tall (jump only if allowed)
exercises.joint_notes: IMPACT when jumping: group sessions use the no jump version (step back, step in, stand). Devil's press and man makers: DB hinge skill required.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 6 x 20 to 40s
exercises.progress_by: Add a press, push up or jump
exercises.regress_by: Step back burpee, incline burpee onto a bench

exercises.name: Step Jacks (No Jump)
exercises.why: Step one foot out to the side as the arms rise overhead, alternate sides. Low impact jumping jack alternative for groups.
cues: Light on the toes
Rhythm
Soft knees
exercises.joint_notes: IMPACT: excluded from group sessions and avoid with pelvic floor symptoms.
exercises.prescription: 30 to 60s
exercises.progress_by: Faster, longer
exercises.regress_by: Step jacks

exercises.name: Marching High Knees
exercises.why: Driving the knees up in a fast march with no hop. A no impact swap for high knees in group warm ups and finishers.
cues: Move through big comfortable ranges
Increase range each rep
Breathe and stay controlled
exercises.joint_notes: Safe for almost everyone.
exercises.prescription: 1 to 2 x 5 to 10 each side (or 20 to 30m)
exercises.progress_by: Bigger range, add reaches
exercises.regress_by: Smaller range, hand support

exercises.name: Zone 2 Steady State (Bike, Rower or Ski)
exercises.muscles: Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
exercises.why: 20 to 45 minutes at a pace where you can just hold a conversation (RPE 3 to 4). Builds the aerobic base, mitochondrial health and fat burning capacity; Peter Attia's longevity foundation. Usually done outside group sessions (walks, cycling) or as recovery.
cues: Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence
Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs
Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips
faults: Going out too hard in intervals
exercises.joint_notes: Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
exercises.prescription: Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
exercises.progress_by: Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds
exercises.regress_by: Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest

exercises.name: VO2 Max Intervals (4 x 4 min)
exercises.muscles: Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
exercises.why: 4 to 5 intervals of 3 to 4 minutes hard (RPE 8 to 9) with equal easy recovery on the bike, rower or ski. Improves peak aerobic capacity, one of the strongest predictors of longevity (Attia). Teams, once per week maximum.
cues: Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence
Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs
Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips
faults: Going out too hard in intervals
exercises.joint_notes: Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
exercises.prescription: Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
exercises.progress_by: Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds
exercises.regress_by: Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest

exercises.name: Sprint Intervals 10 to 20s (Bike or Ski)
exercises.muscles: Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
exercises.why: 6 to 10 all out efforts of 10 to 20 seconds with 1 to 2 minutes easy. Stacy Sims recommends this short, sharp style for peri and post menopausal women; Cosgrove ranks intervals above steady cardio for fat loss. Zero impact on the bike or ski erg.
variation_notes: Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
cues: Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence
Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs
Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips
faults: Going out too hard in intervals
exercises.joint_notes: Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
exercises.prescription: Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
exercises.progress_by: Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds
exercises.regress_by: Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest
same_level_swaps: Zone 2 Steady State (Bike, Rower or Ski)

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift (Low Handles)
exercises.why: The trap bar lets people stand inside the weight with neutral grip, so the load sits in line with the body. Far less low back stress than a straight bar and much easier to learn. DeFranco and Cosgrove's go to heavy lift and Optimal's default heavy deadlift for 40+ (bone density, strength, grip).
cues: Stand in the middle, hinge down and grip the handles
Chest proud, take the slack out of the bar, brace
Push the floor away, stand tall, lower with control
faults: Rounding the back off the floor
Jerking the bar off the floor
exercises.joint_notes: The most joint friendly heavy lift. High handles reduce range for tall members or stiff hips/backs.
exercises.prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8
exercises.progress_by: Add load, low handles, pause just off the floor, rep max progressions (Teams G4)
exercises.regress_by: High handles, KB deadlift from blocks, lighter load

exercises.name: Nordic Curl (Full)
exercises.why: Hamstrings both extend the hip and bend the knee; curls train the knee bending role that RDLs miss. Strong hamstrings protect knees and reduce hamstring strain risk. Nordic curls are among the best researched injury prevention exercises.
cues: Lie on your back, heels on the ball/sliders/TRX, lift the hips
Curl the heels towards the bum keeping the hips high
Extend slowly back out (control is the exercise)
exercises.joint_notes: Knee friendly. Nordics are demanding: use band assistance and partial range, expect soreness at first.
exercises.prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
exercises.progress_by: Hips stay up throughout, single leg, slower lowering, Nordic progression
exercises.regress_by: Hips on the floor curl, eccentric only, double leg
